Page 02 / 11

My mistakes

Hold short · read first

Mistake 01Members vs accessorsLINK

Inside the class: digit_, candidates_, neighboors_. From another class (e.g. Grid): only the public accessors digit(), candidates(), neighboors(). Without the (), the name is the function itself, not its value.

Mistake 02Accessor returning an arrayLINK

cell.neighboors()[i], not cell.neighboors(i).

Mistake 03Pointers use ->LINK

neighboors_ holds Cell*, so nb->prune(guess).

Mistake 04private is per class, not per objectLINK

a Cell can call prune on another Cell. Grid can't, so it uses the public eraseCandidate.

Mistake 05std::vector has no .remove()LINK

Use v.erase(it), and only when it != v.end() (erasing end() crashes). Check for a provided helper first (eraseCandidate does find + erase safely).

Mistake 06Size is .size()LINK

, not .len() (Python).

Mistake 07A 1-D std::array<Cell, 81> used as a gridLINK

cells[9*row + col], not cells[row][col].

Mistake 08Loop index vs .size()LINK

use size_t i or a range-for, otherwise signed/unsigned warning.

Mistake 09if (in == true) is just if (in)LINK

Mistake 10Prefer range-for to index loopsLINK

for (auto &cell : cells)                 // & = no copy (Cell can't be copied anyway)
    if (cell.digit() != 0)
        for (auto nb : cell.neighboors())  // nb is a Cell*
            nb->eraseCandidate(cell.digit());

Mistake 11Order matters in undo functionsLINK

in cancel(), use digit_ (restore on the neighbours) before resetting it to 0.

Mistake 12Backtracking: no return false inside the candidate loopLINK

After cancel(), fall through to the next candidate; return false goes after the loop (all candidates failed). A return inside the loop = only the first candidate is ever tried.

Mistake 13Program "hangs" after an OpenCV window opens?LINK

It is cv::waitKey(0): click the window and press a key in it. (QSettings::value: Empty key passed is harmless Qt noise.)

Mistake 14Backtracking "stuck" on a hard input?LINK

Usually just exponential: pick the most constrained cell first (fewest candidates) and build in Release (cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ..).

Mistake 15vec1 < vec2 compares contents (dictionary order), not lengthsLINK

For "fewer elements", compare vec1.size() < vec2.size().

Mistake 16Comparator for min_elementLINK

returns true if c1 is better. Rule out invalid items first (if (c1.digit()) return false; if (c2.digit()) return true;), then compare.

Mistake 17Bookkeeping lineLINK

prune must increment pruned_count_[guess] "in any case", otherwise restore breaks.

Time plan (2 h)LINK

Time What
0:00 - 0:10 Read the subject PDF and code skeleton. Build the untouched project. git init. Note the TODOs in order.
0:10 - 1:45 Do the TODOs in the subject's order. Commit after each one that works.
1:45 - 2:00 No new features. Clean build, run once, commit. Comment out anything broken.

The last 10 minutes are for "it compiles and is committed", not new code.

Quick gitLINK

cd <project dir>
git init && git add -A && git commit -qm start     # once, after the first build works
git add -A && git commit -qm "step N works"        # after each working method
git log --oneline
git stash                                          # park a broken attempt (git stash pop to restore)
git checkout -- file.cpp                           # throw away edits to one file (careful)

Identity error:

git config user.email "me@x" && git config user.name "me"

Do not commit the build/ folder: echo build/ > .gitignore before git add -A.

Clean buildLINK

rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make -j4
# or: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release ..   (much faster backtracking)
# or: cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug ..     (for gdb)

New .cpp file added? Re-run cmake .. (and check it is in add_executable / the glob).

Working rulesLINK

  • Stuck for more than 10 minutes on a TODO: move on. Leave a // TODO unfinished comment, keep it compiling, come back at the end.
  • The subject PDF has the algorithm pseudocode: translate it line by line, same variable names, order and loop structure. Do not "improve" it.
  • Read only the FIRST compiler error (later ones are often consequences). See compiler_errors.md.
  • Check provided helpers before writing your own (e.g. eraseCandidate, print, distToPrevious).
  • The comments in the provided headers state what each method must do.
  • Print intermediate values (std::cout) instead of guessing; remove noisy prints at the end.
  • Re-read my_mistakes.md once before starting and once at the 1 h mark.
  • find.sh <word> greps the whole stick; 2_snippets/ has backtracking, A* Node, minimax, GA, CMake.

Before handing inLINK

  • [ ] rm -rf build && mkdir build && cd build && cmake .. && make succeeds with no errors.
  • [ ] Program runs and gives a plausible result.
  • [ ] Broken/unfinished code is commented out, not left half-written.
  • [ ] git add -A && git commit -qm final.
  • [ ] No debug prints flooding the output; no waitKey(0) surprises left unexplained.

C++

Compile: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -g main.cpp -o main

Header / source splitLINK

// cell.h
#ifndef CELL_H            // include guard (or: #pragma once)
#define CELL_H
#include <vector>
class Cell {
public:
    Cell(int x, int y);
    int digit() const;
private:
    int digit_ = 0;
};
#endif

// cell.cpp
#include "cell.h"
Cell::Cell(int x, int y) : digit_(0) {}
int Cell::digit() const { return digit_; }
  • Declarations in .h, definitions in .cpp (Class::method). Templates: definitions must stay in the .h.
  • Every .cpp must be listed in CMake add_executable (or a glob) or you get "undefined reference".
  • #include "mine.h" for your files, <vector> for the standard library.
  • Never using namespace std; in a header.
  • uint is a Linux/glibc typedef (unsigned int). On other platforms write unsigned int.

ClassesLINK

class Point {
public:
    Point() = default;
    Point(int x, int y) : x_(x), y_(y) {}       // init list (members init in DECLARATION order)
    explicit Point(int v) : x_(v), y_(v) {}     // no implicit int -> Point
    Point(const Point&) = default;
    Point& operator=(const Point&) = default;
    virtual ~Point() = default;                 // virtual dtor if used polymorphically

    int x() const { return x_; }                // const method: cannot modify members
    void setX(int x) { x_ = x; }
    static int count() { return count_; }       // static: no this, call Point::count()
    friend std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream&, const Point&);  // friend: can see privates
private:
    int x_ = 0, y_ = 0;                         // default member init
    static inline int count_ = 0;               // C++17: static member defined in class
};
  • struct is class with public default.
  • obj.x() for objects/references, ptr->x() (= (*ptr).x()) for pointers.
  • private is per CLASS, not per object: a Cell can touch another Cell's privates.
  • Initialization list is required for const members, reference members and base classes without default ctor.
  • Delete copying: Cell(const Cell&) = delete; -> then use auto& / pointers, never auto.
  • this is a pointer: this->x_, return *this;.
  • Static member function vs member function: static has no this, cannot touch non-static members.

Inheritance, virtualLINK

class Shape {
public:
    virtual ~Shape() = default;
    virtual double area() const = 0;            // pure virtual => abstract class
    virtual void print() const { std::cout << "shape\n"; }
};
class Circle : public Shape {
public:
    Circle(double r) : Shape(), r_(r) {}        // base ctor in init list
    double area() const override { return 3.14159 * r_ * r_; }   // override: compiler checks signature
private:
    double r_;
};
Shape* s = new Circle(2);   s->area();  delete s;      // virtual dispatch through pointer/reference
std::vector<std::unique_ptr<Shape>> v;  v.push_back(std::make_unique<Circle>(1.0));
  • Polymorphism only through pointers/references, not by value (slicing).
  • class Node : public ecn::Point: Node gets Point's public members (x, y).
  • Call the base version: Shape::print();
  • protected: visible to derived classes, hidden from outside.
  • final stops further overriding.

References, pointers, smart pointersLINK

int a = 5;
int& r = a;        // reference: alias, must be initialized, cannot be reseated
int* p = &a;       // pointer: *p is the value; can be nullptr
const int* cp;     // pointer to const int (cannot change *cp)
int* const pc = &a;// const pointer (cannot change pc)
void f(int& out);        // modifies caller's variable
void g(const Big& in);   // read-only, no copy (preferred for big objects)
void h(Big b);           // copy

#include <memory>
auto u = std::make_unique<Cell>(1, 2);   // sole owner, auto-deleted, not copyable
u->digit();   (*u).digit();   u.get();   // u.get() = raw pointer
auto u2 = std::move(u);                  // transfer ownership (u is now null)
auto s = std::make_shared<Cell>(1, 2);   // shared ownership, ref-counted
auto s2 = s;  s.use_count();             // 2
  • Raw new needs delete; arrays new int[n] need delete[]. Prefer vector / smart pointers.
  • Never return a reference/pointer to a local variable (dangling).
  • Pointer to element of a vector dies on push_back realloc.
  • nullptr not NULL/0.

const correctnessLINK

int Cell::digit() const;                   // const method: callable on const objects
const std::vector<int>& cands() const;     // read-only view, no copy
for (const auto& c : cells) c.digit();     // const object => only const methods allowed

"passing const X as this discards qualifiers" = non-const method called on a const object. Mark the method const (if it does not modify) or drop const from the variable.

Operator overloadingLINK

struct P {
    int x, y;
    bool operator==(const P& o) const { return x == o.x && y == o.y; }
    bool operator!=(const P& o) const { return !(*this == o); }
    bool operator<(const P& o) const { return std::tie(x, y) < std::tie(o.x, o.y); } // for set/map/sort
    P operator+(const P& o) const { return {x + o.x, y + o.y}; }
    P& operator+=(const P& o) { x += o.x; y += o.y; return *this; }
    int& operator[](size_t i) { return i == 0 ? x : y; }              // read/write
    const int& operator[](size_t i) const { return i == 0 ? x : y; }  // const version
};
std::ostream& operator<<(std::ostream& os, const P& p) { return os << '(' << p.x << ',' << p.y << ')'; }
  • std::tie needs <tuple>. std::set<P> / std::map<P,..> / std::sort need operator< (or a comparator).
  • unordered_set<P> needs operator== AND a hash.
  • operator<< is a free function (or friend), first arg std::ostream&, return the stream.

LambdasLINK

auto sq = [](int x) { return x * x; };
int k = 3;
auto byVal  = [k](int x) { return x + k; };     // copy of k
auto byRef  = [&k](int x) { k += x; };          // reference to k
auto allRef = [&](int x) { k += x; };           // everything by reference
auto allVal = [=](int x) { return x + k; };     // everything by copy (read-only unless mutable)
auto mut    = [k](int x) mutable { k += x; return k; };
// inside a member function:
auto m = [this](int x) { return x + member_; }; // captures the this pointer
auto cmp = [](const Cell& a, const Cell& b) { return a.candidates().size() < b.candidates().size(); };
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int a, int b) { return a > b; });
auto r = [](int a) -> double { return a / 2.0; };  // explicit return type
  • Do not capture by reference something that dies before the lambda runs.
  • Generic lambda: [](auto a, auto b) { return a < b; }.

auto, structured bindings, range-forLINK

auto x = 5;            // int
auto d = 5.0;          // double
auto s = std::string("a");
auto  c = cells[0];    // COPY (fails if non-copyable)
auto& c = cells[0];    // reference, no copy
const auto& c = cells[0];

std::map<std::string,int> m;
for (const auto& [key, val] : m) std::cout << key << val;   // structured binding
auto [it, inserted] = m.insert({"a", 1});
std::pair<int,int> pr{1,2};  auto [a, b] = pr;

for (int v : vec) {}            // copy of each element (modifying v changes nothing)
for (int& v : vec) v *= 2;      // modify in place
for (const auto& v : vec) {}    // read-only, no copy (default choice for big types)
for (auto nb : cell.neighboors()) // fine when elements are pointers (copying a pointer is cheap)
  • auto drops & and const: use auto& / const auto& explicitly.

TemplatesLINK

template <typename T>
T maxOf(T a, T b) { return a < b ? b : a; }
maxOf(3, 4);  maxOf<double>(3, 4.5);

template <typename T, int N = 3>
class Stack {
public:
    void push(const T& t) { data_.push_back(t); }
    T pop() { T t = data_.back(); data_.pop_back(); return t; }
    bool empty() const { return data_.empty(); }
private:
    std::vector<T> data_;
};
Stack<int> s;  s.push(1);

Generic A*: template <class Node> ... AStar(Node start, Node goal) calls node.neighboors(), node.distToPrevious(), node == goal, node.h(goal), node.print(next). Node must provide exactly those.

// requires a member `std::vector<Node> neighboors() const`
template <class N>
void expand(const N& n) { for (const auto& nb : n.neighboors()) { /* ... */ } }
  • Template code lives entirely in headers.
  • Error messages are long: read the first line and the "required from here" line.

std::functionLINK

#include <functional>
std::function<int(int,int)> op = [](int a, int b) { return a + b; };
op = std::plus<int>();                 // any callable
int apply(std::function<int(int)> f, int x) { return f(x); }
std::function<double(const Node&)> heuristic;   // stored callback

Slower than a template parameter / auto, but storable in members and containers.

enumsLINK

enum class Dir { Up, Down, Left, Right };   // scoped: Dir::Up, no implicit int
Dir d = Dir::Left;
int i = static_cast<int>(d);
Dir e = static_cast<Dir>(2);
switch (d) { case Dir::Up: break; default: break; }
enum Color { Red, Green };                  // old style: Red is an int, pollutes scope

CastingLINK

double d = static_cast<double>(a) / b;
int i = static_cast<int>(3.9);              // 3 (truncates)
size_t n = static_cast<size_t>(i);
// reinterpret_cast (bit reinterpretation), const_cast (remove const), dynamic_cast (checked downcast, needs virtual):
if (auto* c = dynamic_cast<Circle*>(shapePtr)) { /* it is a Circle */ }

Avoid C casts (int)x: they hide bugs.

Arithmetic pitfallsLINK

5 / 2        // 2   (integer division truncates toward zero)
5 / 2.0      // 2.5
-5 / 2       // -2
5 % 3        // 2
-5 % 3       // -2   (sign follows the dividend!)  positive modulo: ((a % n) + n) % n
double avg = sum / n;            // WRONG if both int: use static_cast<double>(sum) / n
1 / 3 * 3.0  // 0   (1/3 is integer 0)

unsigned int a = 3, b = 5;
a - b;                     // 4294967294, NOT -2 (wraps around)
std::vector<int> v;
v.size() - 1;              // huge number when v is empty!
for (size_t i = v.size() - 1; i >= 0; --i) {}   // INFINITE LOOP: size_t >= 0 is always true
for (size_t i = v.size(); i-- > 0; ) {}         // correct reverse loop
for (int i = 0; i < (int)v.size(); ++i) {}      // or cast to avoid signed/unsigned warning
if (i < v.size())          // warning "comparison of signed and unsigned" if i is int
  • abs(int) vs std::abs(double): include <cmath>/<cstdlib> and call std::abs. Plain abs(-2.5) may truncate to int.
  • Float equality: compare with epsilon std::abs(a-b) < 1e-9.
  • int overflow around 2.1e9: use long long for big sums / factorials.
  • char arithmetic: 'a' + 1 is int; c - '0' converts a digit char to int.
  • = vs == in if.
  • Uninitialized locals (int x;) hold garbage.

STL

Which containerLINK

ContainerAccess [i]Add at endInsert middleFindEraseNote
vectorO(1)O(1)*O(n)O(n)O(n)default choice; contiguous
arrayO(1)n/an/aO(n)n/afixed size, stack
dequeO(1)O(1)O(n)O(n)O(n)push/pop both ends
listO(n)O(1)O(1)O(n)O(1)only with an iterator in hand
set / mapO(log n)O(log n)O(log n)O(log n)O(log n)sorted, unique keys
unordered_set / mapO(1)O(1)O(1)O(1)O(1)average; needs hash
priority_queuetop O(1)O(log n)n/an/apop O(log n)max-heap by default
queue / stackfront O(1)O(1)n/an/apop O(1)adapters

* amortised. unordered_* average case.

Iterator invalidationLINK

Container Operation Invalidates
vector push_back / insert / emplace ALL iterators/pointers/refs if it reallocates (size > capacity), else those after the point
vector erase(it) it and everything after (use the returned iterator)
vector resize/reserve beyond capacity all
deque insert/erase in the middle all; push_front/back invalidates iterators but not references
list, map, set insert nothing
list, map, set erase(it) only it (use it = c.erase(it))
unordered_* insert causing rehash iterators (references to elements stay valid)

Do not push_back to a vector inside a range-for over it; do not keep &v[0] / Cell* across a push_back; never erase(v.end()); never dereference end().

vector #include <vector>LINK

std::vector<int> v;
std::vector<int> v(5, 0);           // 5 zeros
std::vector<int> v{1,2,3};
std::vector<std::vector<int>> g(R, std::vector<int>(C, 0));   // R x C grid

v.push_back(4);
v.emplace_back(4);     // constructs in place (v.emplace_back(x, y) for a struct ctor)
v.pop_back();
v.back();  v.front();  // UB if empty
v[i];  v.at(i);        // at() throws out_of_range, [] does not check
v.size();  v.empty();  v.clear();
v.resize(10);          // new elements value-initialized
v.reserve(100);        // capacity only, size unchanged (v[i] still invalid!)
v.insert(v.begin() + 2, 99);        // before index 2
v.insert(v.end(), w.begin(), w.end());   // append another vector
v.erase(v.begin() + 2);
v.erase(v.begin() + 1, v.begin() + 3);   // erase range [1,3)
v.begin(); v.end();  v.rbegin(); v.rend();   // end() is ONE PAST the last element

Erase by value (erase-remove idiom), vector has no .remove():

v.erase(std::remove(v.begin(), v.end(), 5), v.end());                 // all 5s
v.erase(std::remove_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x){ return x < 0; }), v.end());
// first occurrence only:
auto it = std::find(v.begin(), v.end(), 5);
if (it != v.end()) v.erase(it);     // NEVER erase(v.end())

Erase inside a loop:

for (auto it = v.begin(); it != v.end(); ) {
    if (*it < 0) it = v.erase(it);  // returns next valid iterator
    else ++it;
}

Fast unordered delete: std::swap(v[i], v.back()); v.pop_back();

array #include <array>LINK

std::array<int, 5> a{};      // on stack, zero-initialized with {}
a.size(); a[i]; a.fill(0); a.begin(); a.end();
std::array<Cell, 81> cells;  // size is part of the type; passes by value unless &

deque / listLINK

#include <deque>
std::deque<int> d;  d.push_front(1);  d.push_back(2);  d.pop_front();  d.front(); d.back(); d[i];
#include <list>
std::list<int> l;   l.push_back(1);  l.push_front(0);  l.remove(5);   // list HAS remove(value)
l.erase(it);        l.sort();  l.reverse();   // no l[i]

map / unordered_map #include <map> / <unordered_map>LINK

std::map<std::string,int> m;             // sorted, O(log n), key needs operator<
std::unordered_map<std::string,int> um;  // O(1) avg, unordered, key needs hash and ==

m["a"] = 1;                 // operator[] INSERTS default value if key missing!
m["zzz"];                   // creates "zzz" -> 0  (use find/count to only look)
m.insert({"b", 2});         // no-op if key exists, returns pair<iterator,bool>
m.emplace("c", 3);
m.at("a");                  // throws if missing, does not insert
m.count("a");               // 0 or 1
auto it = m.find("a");      // m.end() if missing
if (it != m.end()) { it->first; it->second; }
m.erase("a");               // or m.erase(it)
m.size(); m.empty(); m.clear();
for (const auto& [k, v] : m) std::cout << k << v;      // sorted for map
for (auto& kv : m) kv.second++;                        // kv is pair<const K,V>

Frequency count: for (char c : s) ++freq[c]; Key = struct: define operator< (map) or hash (unordered_map). A std::pair<int,int> key works with map directly, not with unordered_map.

set / unordered_setLINK

std::set<int> s{3,1,2};      // sorted, unique, O(log n)
s.insert(4);  s.erase(4);  s.count(4);  s.find(4) != s.end();
*s.begin();  *s.rbegin();    // min / max
s.lower_bound(2);            // first >= 2
std::unordered_set<int> us;  us.insert(1);  us.count(1);   // O(1) avg
std::set<std::pair<int,int>> visited;  visited.insert({x,y});

Visited-set pattern: if (!visited.insert(state).second) continue; (.second is false if already present).

pair / tupleLINK

#include <utility>
std::pair<int,std::string> p{1, "a"};  p.first; p.second;  auto p2 = std::make_pair(1, 2);
p < q            // lexicographic compare
#include <tuple>
std::tuple<int,double,char> t{1, 2.0, 'c'};
std::get<0>(t);  auto [a,b,c] = t;  std::tie(a,b,c) = t;

priority_queue #include <queue>LINK

std::priority_queue<int> maxpq;                                   // MAX-heap by default (top = largest)
std::priority_queue<int, std::vector<int>, std::greater<int>> minpq;   // MIN-heap
pq.push(x);  pq.top();  pq.pop();  pq.empty();  pq.size();        // pop() returns void: read top() first

Pairs: priority_queue<pair<double,int>, vector<...>, greater<...>> pops smallest cost first.

Custom comparator struct (inverted: the element for which cmp is "less" sinks, so use > for a min-heap on cost):

struct Cmp {
    bool operator()(const Node& a, const Node& b) const { return a.f() > b.f(); }  // smallest f on top
};
std::priority_queue<Node, std::vector<Node>, Cmp> open;

Lambda comparator:

auto cmp = [](const Node& a, const Node& b) { return a.f() > b.f(); };
std::priority_queue<Node, std::vector<Node>, decltype(cmp)> open(cmp);

No decrease-key: push a duplicate with the better cost, skip stale entries when popped (if (closed.count(n)) continue;).

queue / stackLINK

std::queue<int> q;  q.push(1); q.front(); q.back(); q.pop(); q.empty(); q.size();   // BFS (FIFO)
std::stack<int> st; st.push(1); st.top();   st.pop(); st.empty();                   // DFS (LIFO)

pop() returns nothing: int x = q.front(); q.pop();

string #include <string>LINK

std::string s = "hello world";
s.size(); s.length(); s.empty(); s[0]; s.back(); s.front();
s.substr(pos, len);          // s.substr(6) = "world", s.substr(0,5) = "hello"
s.find("lo");                // std::string::npos if missing

#include <sstream>
std::vector<std::string> split(const std::string& line, char sep) {

}

min_element / max_element

auto it = std::min_element(v.begin(), v.end());                 // uses <
auto it = std::min_element(v.begin(), v.end(),
        [](const Cell& a, const Cell& b) { return a.candidates().size() < b.candidates().size(); });
  • comp(a, b) returns true if a is "better"/smaller than b.
  • Returns an ITERATOR: *it, it->member, std::distance(v.begin(), it) for the index. Empty range returns end().
  • Rule out invalid items first:
[](const Cell& a, const Cell& b) {
    if (a.digit()) return false;     // a already filled: never better
    if (b.digit()) return true;      // b filled: a is better
    return a.candidates().size() < b.candidates().size();
}
  • max_element: same comp, returns the element no other is "greater" than.
  • For a container of non-copyable objects, take const auto& params.

priority_queuecustom comparator declarationLINK

std::priority_queue<T, std::vector<T>, Cmp> pq;

std::priority_queue<T, std::vector<T>, decltype(cmp)> pq(cmp);

std::priority_queue<std::pair<int,int>, std::vector<std::pair<int,int>>, decltype(cmp)> pq(cmp);
pq.push({1, 9}); pq.push({2, 3});   // top() is {2,3}: smallest .second
<queue>

Comparator is inverted vs sort: cmp(a,b) true means a has LOWER priority (a comes out after b). With '>' you get a min-heap. The lambda form needs pq(cmp) in the constructor.

Equals (size_t)-1, the 'not found' value of find/rfind.

algorithmsortLINK

void std::sort(It first, It last);
void std::sort(It first, It last, Compare comp);

std::vector<int> v{3,1,2};
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end());                          // {1,2,3}
std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), std::greater<int>());     // {3,2,1}
<algorithm>, <functional>O(n log n)

Needs random-access iterators: not std::list (use l.sort()). comp must be a strict order (< or >, never <= or >=), otherwise UB/crash.

algorithmstable_sortLINK

void std::stable_sort(It first, It last[, Compare comp]);

std::vector<std::pair<int,int>> v{{2,1},{1,2},{2,0}};
std::stable_sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](auto& a, auto& b){ return a.first < b.first; });
<algorithm>O(n log n)

Keeps the original order of equal elements.

algorithmsort with lambdaLINK

std::sort(first, last, [](const T& a, const T& b) { return <a goes before b>; });

std::sort(v.begin(), v.end(), [](const auto& a, const auto& b) { return a.second < b.second; });

comp(a,b) returns true if a must come BEFORE b (a is better/smaller). Ascending uses <.

std::reverse(v.begin(), v.end());   // {3,2,1}

In place; returns nothing.

if (it != v.end()) { int idx = it - v.begin(); }   // idx = 1
<algorithm>O(n)

Returns last (v.end()) if not found. Index = it - v.begin().

algorithmfind_ifLINK

It std::find_if(It first, It last, Pred p);

Returns last if none matches.

algorithmcountLINK

<algorithm>O(n)

algorithmcount_ifLINK

auto c = std::count_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x){ return x % 2 == 0; });   // 2

Returns an ITERATOR (dereference for the value). Returns last if empty: dereferencing then is UB. First of equal minima.

algorithmmax_elementLINK

auto it = std::max_element(v.begin(), v.end());
int m = *it, idx = it - v.begin();   // 3, 0

Returns an ITERATOR. Returns last if empty. First of equal maxima. comp(a,b) true means a < b.

One pass; returns {min iterator, max iterator}. For ties, min is the first and max is the LAST.

algorithmminLINK

const T& std::min(const T& a, const T& b[, Compare comp]);

const T& std::max(const T& a, const T& b[, Compare comp]);

Both arguments must have the SAME type. Returns a reference: do not keep it bound to a temporary.

C++17. Argument order is (value, low, high). UB if lo > hi.

algorithmswapLINK

algorithmtransformLINK

algorithmremove (erase-remove idiom)LINK

It std::remove(It first, It last, const T& val);
v.erase(std::remove(v.begin(), v.end(), val), v.end());

std::remove alone only shuffles elements and returns the new logical end; the vector keeps its size until you erase(it, end).

algorithmremove_ifLINK

algorithmuniqueLINK

Removes only CONSECUTIVE duplicates: sort first. Like remove, it needs .erase(...) afterwards.

algorithmany_ofLINK

algorithmall_ofLINK

algorithmnone_ofLINK

algorithmlower_boundLINK

It std::lower_bound(It first, It last, const T& val[, Compare comp]);

algorithmupper_boundLINK

utility / tuplepair / make_pairLINK

Comparison is lexicographic (first, then second), so sort/set/map work on pairs.

utility / tupletuple / make_tupleLINK

Access with std::get<I>(t), not t.first.

utility / tupletieLINK

utility / tuplegetLINK

utility / tuplestructured bindingLINK

std::pair<int,double> p{1, 2.5};

C++17. Declares new variables; auto& binds by reference so changes write through.

utility / tuplemoveLINK

Only casts to an rvalue; the move happens in the receiving constructor/assignment. Do not use the moved-from object (except to assign/destroy).

utility / tupleswapLINK

cmathhypotLINK

cmathfloor / ceil / roundLINK

double std::ceil(double x);
double std::round(double x);
long std::lround(double x);

double b = std::ceil(2.1);    // 3.0

iostream / sstream

iostream / sstreamcout with setprecisionLINK

std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(n) << x;
std::cout << std::setw(n) << x;

double x = 3.14159;
std::cout << std::fixed << std::setprecision(2) << x << "\n";   // 3.14
<iostream>, <iomanip>

With std::fixed, n counts digits AFTER the point; without it, n counts significant digits. Both stick to the stream until changed. Prefer "\n" to std::endl (which flushes).

iostream / sstreamcinLINK

std::cin >> a >> b;
while (std::cin >> x) { ... }

int a, b;
std::cin >> a >> b;
double x;
while (std::cin >> x) { }   // until EOF or bad input

Segfault / crash causes (runtime)LINK

Segmentation fault (core dumped), terminate called after throwing an instance of 'std::out_of_range', free(): invalid pointer, double free, stack smashing detected.

  • Index out of range: v[i] with i >= size(), v[-1], cells[9*row+col] out of bounds, v.size() - 1 on empty vector (unsigned wrap), back()/front()/pop_back() on empty.
  • Dangling pointer/reference: pointer to a local that went out of scope; reference or Cell* into a vector that then reallocated on push_back; reference to a temporary.
  • Iterator invalidation: erase or push_back inside a range-for over the same vector; using it after v.erase(it) (use it = v.erase(it)).
  • erase(v.end()): find returned end() and it was erased without checking it != v.end().
  • Dereferencing null / end(): *min_element(...) on an empty range, map.find(k)->second when k absent.
  • Infinite recursion (stack overflow shows as Segmentation fault): missing base case in backtracking or minimax. Check the depth test (if (depth == 0 || gameOver) return eval;).
  • Uninitialized pointer/variable: Cell* p; p->digit();
  • Deleting twice, or mixing new[] with delete. Use smart pointers / vectors.
  • Infinite loop (not a crash): unsigned >= 0 loop, forgot ++, A* with no closed set, waitKey(0) waiting for a key (click window, press a key).
  • Unreachable goal / endless search: state not marked visited; neighbours not filtered by walls.

Page 08 / 11

Algorithms

Which algorithmLINK

Fill a grid / assign values under constraints (sudoku, N-queens, KenKen)?Backtrackingset a value -> recurse -> cancel. Pick the most constrained cell first.
Shortest sequence of moves to a goal, with a distance estimate (maze, 15-puzzle)?A*Needs neighboors(), distToPrevious(), h(goal). h must never overestimate.
Shortest path where every move costs 1 and no heuristic is given?BFSQueue + visited. First time you reach the goal = shortest.
Explore everything / count regions / reachability?DFS / flood fillRecursive or with a stack. Mark visited before recursing.
Two players taking turns (Connect Four, Nim, tic-tac-toe)?Minimax + alpha-betaplay -> recurse -> undo. Score from the side to move (negamax).
Optimise an ordering / parameters with no exact method (TSP)?Genetic algorithmFitness, selection, crossover that keeps a valid permutation, mutation.
Same sub-problem computed again and again (counting ways, Fibonacci)?Recursion + memoCache results keyed by the arguments.

01BacktrackingLINK

solve():
  if everything assigned: return true
  x = most constrained open variable      // fewest candidates
  for v in candidates(x):                  // iterate over a COPY
      set(x, v)                            // + prune v from neighbours
      if solve(): return true
      cancel(x)                            // undo EXACTLY what set did
  return false                             // all candidates failed
Sudoku (past exam)Snippet

You implement

  • set / cancel (and prune / restore with a counter)
  • is-complete check
  • comparator for min_element (best next cell)

Classic bugs

  • return false INSIDE the loop (only first candidate tried)
  • cancel() not restoring what set() pruned
  • comparator letting already-filled cells win

Exponential worst case; the heuristic decides the speed.

02A* searchLINK

open = {start};  g[start] = 0
while open not empty:
    cur = node in open with smallest f = g + h(cur, goal)
    if cur == goal: return path (follow parent)
    move cur from open to closed
    for nb in cur.neighboors():
        if nb in closed: continue
        ng = g[cur] + nb.distToPrevious()
        if nb not in open or ng < g[nb]:
            g[nb] = ng;  parent[nb] = cur;  put nb in open
return no path
Maze (past exam)Snippet

You implement

  • neighboors(): only valid, free positions
  • distToPrevious() when moves can be longer than 1
  • h(goal): Manhattan on grids (never overestimate)
  • operator== comparing the state

Classic bugs

  • neighbours going through walls / out of the grid
  • h overestimating -> path not shortest
  • operator== comparing the wrong fields

Explores far fewer nodes than BFS with a good h.

03BFS / DFSLINK

BFS(start):                              DFS(u):
  queue = {start}; visited = {start}        visited.insert(u)
  while queue not empty:                    for v in neighbours(u):
      u = queue.front(); queue.pop()            if v not visited:
      for v in neighbours(u):                       DFS(v)
          if v not visited:
              visited.insert(v)   // mark when PUSHING
              parent[v] = u
              queue.push(v)
Building block (maze, regions)Snippet

You implement

  • neighbours on a grid: 4 directions, bounds check
  • visited as vector<vector<bool>> or set

Classic bugs

  • marking visited when popping (duplicates in the queue)
  • row/column swapped (x = column, y = row)

O(V + E). BFS = shortest path when all moves cost 1.

04Minimax + alpha-betaLINK

negamax(state, depth, alpha, beta):
    if depth == 0 or state.isTerminal():
        return evaluate(state)            // from the side to move
    best = -INF
    for m in state.validMoves():
        state.play(m)
        score = -negamax(state, depth-1, -beta, -alpha)
        state.undo(m)
        best  = max(best, score)
        alpha = max(alpha, score)
        if alpha >= beta: break           // prune
    return best
Likely: Connect Four / NimSnippet

You implement

  • validMoves / play / undo (like set / cancel)
  • isTerminal + evaluate (sign = side to move)
  • bestMove() looping over root moves

Classic bugs

  • forgetting undo() after the recursive call
  • evaluate from the wrong player's view (sign)
  • not negating AND swapping alpha/beta

b^d without pruning; about b^(d/2) with good move order.

05Genetic algorithmLINK

pop = N random permutations
repeat G generations:
    sort pop by fitness;  keep E elites
    while new_pop not full:
        a = tournament(pop);  b = tournament(pop)
        child = orderCrossover(a, b)      // stays a valid permutation
        if rand() < p_mut: mutate(child)  // swap or inversion
        new_pop.push_back(child)
    pop = new_pop
return best individual
Likely: TSPSnippet

You implement

  • fitness (tour length: lower = better)
  • selection (tournament of k)
  • crossover keeping a permutation (OX)
  • mutation (swap / reverse a segment)

Classic bugs

  • crossover producing duplicates (city visited twice)
  • minimising vs maximising mixed up
  • no elitism -> best solution lost

No optimality guarantee; tune population / generations.

06Recursion + memoLINK

f(args):
    if base case: return value
    if args in memo: return memo[args]
    r = combine( f(smaller args) ... )
    memo[args] = r
    return r
Building block (Hanoi, counting)Snippet

You implement

  • base case first
  • memo keyed by the arguments

Classic bugs

  • missing base case (stack overflow / segfault)
  • memo key missing an argument

Memo turns exponential into (number of distinct args) x work.

  1// backtracking.cpp - generic recursive backtracking with the set / cancel (undo) pattern.
  2// Build: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 backtracking.cpp -o backtracking
  3//
  4// Pattern (same as the sudoku exam: Cell::set / cancel, Grid::solveNextCell):
  5//   solve(state):
  6//     if state is complete          -> return true
  7//     pick the next decision point  (cell / row / variable)
  8//     for each candidate value:
  9//         state.set(decision, value)       // modify the state (and prune the others)
 10//         if solve(state) return true      // go deeper
 11//         state.cancel(decision, value)    // UNDO exactly what set() did
 12//     return false                         // dead end: caller will try its next value
 13//
 14// Golden rule: cancel() must restore the state EXACTLY as before set().
 15#include <algorithm>
 16#include <iostream>
 17#include <vector>
 18
 19// Part 1: N-queens as a concrete problem. One queen per row, we choose a column.
 20class Queens
 21{
 22public:
 23    explicit Queens(int n)
 24        : n_(n), col_(static_cast<size_t>(n), -1),
 25          usedCol_(static_cast<size_t>(n), false),
 26          usedDiag1_(static_cast<size_t>(2 * n), false),
 27          usedDiag2_(static_cast<size_t>(2 * n), false) {}
 28
 29    int size() const { return n_; }
 30    int columnOf(int row) const { return col_[static_cast<size_t>(row)]; }
 31
 32    bool canSet(int row, int c) const
 33    {
 34        return !usedCol_[static_cast<size_t>(c)]
 35            && !usedDiag1_[static_cast<size_t>(row + c)]
 36            && !usedDiag2_[static_cast<size_t>(row - c + n_)];
 37    }
 38
 39    void set(int row, int c)
 40    {
 41        col_[static_cast<size_t>(row)] = c;
 42        usedCol_[static_cast<size_t>(c)] = true;
 43        usedDiag1_[static_cast<size_t>(row + c)] = true;
 44        usedDiag2_[static_cast<size_t>(row - c + n_)] = true;
 45    }
 46
 47    void cancel(int row, int c)
 48    {
 49        col_[static_cast<size_t>(row)] = -1;
 50        usedCol_[static_cast<size_t>(c)] = false;
 51        usedDiag1_[static_cast<size_t>(row + c)] = false;
 52        usedDiag2_[static_cast<size_t>(row - c + n_)] = false;
 53    }
 54
 55    void print() const
 56    {
 57        for(int r = 0; r < n_; ++r)
 58        {
 59            for(int c = 0; c < n_; ++c)
 60                std::cout << (col_[static_cast<size_t>(r)] == c ? "Q " : ". ");
 61            std::cout << "\n";
 62        }
 63    }
 64
 65private:
 66    int n_;
 67    std::vector<int> col_;
 68    std::vector<bool> usedCol_, usedDiag1_, usedDiag2_;
 69};
 70
 71// First solution only.
 72// ADAPT: replace Queens by your state type, 'row' by your decision point and
 73// the loop over columns by the loop over candidate values.
 74bool solveFirst(Queens &q, int row)
 75{
 76    if(row == q.size())            // ADAPT: "state complete" test
 77        return true;
 78
 79    for(int c = 0; c < q.size(); ++c)   // ADAPT: candidates for this decision
 80    {
 81        if(!q.canSet(row, c))
 82            continue;
 83        q.set(row, c);
 84        if(solveFirst(q, row + 1))
 85            return true;           // keep the state as is: it IS the solution
 86        q.cancel(row, c);
 87    }
 88    return false;
 89}
 90
 91// All solutions: do not return on success, just count (and undo anyway).
 92int countAll(Queens &q, int row)
 93{
 94    if(row == q.size())
 95        return 1;
 96    int total = 0;
 97    for(int c = 0; c < q.size(); ++c)
 98    {
 99        if(!q.canSet(row, c))
100            continue;
101        q.set(row, c);
102        total += countAll(q, row + 1);
103        q.cancel(row, c);          // always cancel when searching for everything
104    }
105    return total;
106}
107
108// Part 2: generic skeleton (template) to copy. State must provide:
109//   bool complete() const;
110//   bool pickDecision(Decision &d) const;           // false if nothing left
111//   std::vector<Value> candidates(const Decision&) const;
112//   void set(const Decision&, const Value&);
113//   void cancel(const Decision&, const Value&);
114template<class State, class Decision, class Value>
115bool backtrack(State &s)
116{
117    if(s.complete())
118        return true;
119    Decision d;
120    if(!s.pickDecision(d))
121        return false;
122    for(const Value &v : s.candidates(d))
123    {
124        s.set(d, v);
125        if(backtrack<State, Decision, Value>(s))
126            return true;
127        s.cancel(d, v);
128    }
129    return false;
130}
131
132// Part 3: "most constrained first" heuristic (sudoku exam: min_element).
133// Instead of taking the next cell in order, pick the undecided cell with the
134// FEWEST remaining candidates: failures are discovered much earlier.
135//
136//   std::vector<Cell*> todo = ...undecided cells...;
137//   auto it = std::min_element(todo.begin(), todo.end(),
138//       [](const Cell *a, const Cell *b){ return a->candidates() < b->candidates(); });
139//   if (it == todo.end()) return true;   // nothing left -> solved
140//   Cell *c = *it;
141//   // ADAPT: try each candidate of *c with set / recurse / cancel.
142//
143// Tiny runnable version below: pick the row with fewest legal columns.
144int legalCount(const Queens &q, int row)
145{
146    int k = 0;
147    for(int c = 0; c < q.size(); ++c)
148        if(q.canSet(row, c))
149            ++k;
150    return k;
151}
152
153bool solveMostConstrained(Queens &q, std::vector<int> &rowsLeft)
154{
155    if(rowsLeft.empty())
156        return true;
157    // ADAPT: comparator = "which decision is the most constrained"
158    auto it = std::min_element(rowsLeft.begin(), rowsLeft.end(),
159        [&q](int a, int b) { return legalCount(q, a) < legalCount(q, b); });
160    const int row = *it;
161    rowsLeft.erase(it);                      // remove from the todo list...
162    for(int c = 0; c < q.size(); ++c)
163    {
164        if(!q.canSet(row, c))
165            continue;
166        q.set(row, c);
167        if(solveMostConstrained(q, rowsLeft))
168            return true;
169        q.cancel(row, c);
170    }
171    rowsLeft.push_back(row);                 // ...and restore it when backtracking
172    return false;
173}
174
175int main()
176{
177    Queens q(8);
178    if(solveFirst(q, 0))
179    {
180        std::cout << "First solution of 8-queens:\n";
181        q.print();
182    }
183
184    Queens q2(8);
185    std::cout << "Number of solutions for 8 queens: " << countAll(q2, 0)
186              << " (expected 92)\n";
187
188    Queens q3(8);
189    std::vector<int> rows;
190    for(int r = 0; r < 8; ++r)
191        rows.push_back(r);
192    std::cout << "Most-constrained-first solve: "
193              << (solveMostConstrained(q3, rows) ? "found" : "none") << "\n";
194    return 0;
195}

  1// astar.cpp - self-contained generic A* (template) + 8-puzzle demo.
  2// Build: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 astar.cpp -o astar
  3//
  4// Professor's Node interface (maze/include/a_star.h, note the spelling "neighboors"):
  5//     std::vector<Node> neighboors() const;     // successors of this state
  6//     int  distToPrevious() const;              // cost of the step that led here (1 on grids)
  7//     bool operator==(const Node &other) const; // same state?
  8//     double h(const Node &goal) const;         // admissible heuristic (never overestimates)
  9//
 10// Two flavours:
 11//   astar(start, goal)             needs ONLY the interface above (linear lookup, simple, slow
 12//                                  when many nodes are generated)
 13//   astarKeyed(start, goal, key)   same + a key function Node -> std::string (or int, pair...)
 14//                                  so duplicate detection is O(log n). Use for puzzles.
 15//
 16// ecn::Astar plug-in: search "USE_ECN_ASTAR".
 17#include <algorithm>

 20#include <cstdlib>

 29namespace astar_snip
 30{
 31
 32struct Stats
 33{
 34    size_t expanded = 0;   // nodes popped and expanded
 35    size_t generated = 0;  // nodes created by neighboors()
 36};
 37
 38// Open-set entry. f = g + h.
 39struct OpenEntry
 40{
 41    double f;
 42    int g;
 43    size_t idx;   // index into the "nodes" vector
 44};
 45
 46// priority_queue is a max-heap, so "less" means "worse": larger f is worse;
 47// on equal f prefer the deeper node (larger g), it usually finds the goal faster.
 48struct OpenWorse
 49{
 50    bool operator()(const OpenEntry &a, const OpenEntry &b) const
 51    {
 52        if(a.f != b.f)
 53            return a.f > b.f;
 54        return a.g < b.g;
 55    }
 56};
 57
 58// Duplicate lookup #1: only needs operator== (linear search).
 59template<class Node>
 60struct LinearIndex
 61{
 62    static constexpr size_t npos = static_cast<size_t>(-1);
 63    size_t find(const std::vector<Node> &nodes, const Node &n) const
 64    {
 65        for(size_t i = 0; i < nodes.size(); ++i)
 66            if(nodes[i] == n)          // ADAPT: uses Node::operator==
 67                return i;
 68        return npos;
 69    }
 70    void add(const Node &, size_t) {}
 71};
 72
 73// Duplicate lookup #2: ordered map from a key to the node index.
 74template<class Node, class KeyFn>
 75struct MapIndex
 76{
 77    using Key = std::decay_t<decltype(std::declval<KeyFn>()(std::declval<Node>()))>;
 78    static constexpr size_t npos = static_cast<size_t>(-1);
 79    explicit MapIndex(KeyFn k) : key(std::move(k)) {}
 80    size_t find(const std::vector<Node> &, const Node &n) const
 81    {
 82        auto it = table.find(key(n));
 83        return it == table.end() ? npos : it->second;
 84    }
 85    void add(const Node &n, size_t idx) { table[key(n)] = idx; }
 86    KeyFn key;
 87    std::map<Key, size_t> table;
 88};
 89
 90// Index = LinearIndex or MapIndex.
 91// Returns the path start..goal (empty vector if no solution).
 92template<class Node, class Index>
 93std::vector<Node> core(const Node &start, const Node &goal, Index &index, Stats *stats)
 94{
 95    const size_t npos = static_cast<size_t>(-1);
 96    std::vector<Node> nodes;           // owner of every state ever created
 97    std::vector<size_t> parent;        // parent[i] = index of the node we came from
 98    std::vector<int> gCost;            // best known cost from start to nodes[i]
 99    std::vector<double> hCost;         // cached heuristic (computed once per node)
100    std::vector<char> closed;          // 1 = already expanded with its best g
101    std::priority_queue<OpenEntry, std::vector<OpenEntry>, OpenWorse> open;
102
103    nodes.push_back(start);
104    parent.push_back(npos);
105    gCost.push_back(0);
106    hCost.push_back(start.h(goal));
107    closed.push_back(0);
108    index.add(start, 0);
109    open.push(OpenEntry{hCost[0], 0, 0});
110
111    while(!open.empty())
112    {
113        const OpenEntry cur = open.top();
114        open.pop();
115        // lazy deletion: skip stale entries (a cheaper path was found meanwhile)
116        if(cur.g > gCost[cur.idx] || closed[cur.idx])
117            continue;
118        closed[cur.idx] = 1;
119        if(stats)
120            ++stats->expanded;
121
122        if(nodes[cur.idx] == goal)     // goal test when POPPED -> optimal path
123        {
124            std::vector<Node> path;
125            for(size_t i = cur.idx; i != npos; i = parent[i])
126                path.push_back(nodes[i]);
127            std::reverse(path.begin(), path.end());
128            return path;
129        }
130
131        // copy: 'nodes' may reallocate while we push below
132        const Node here = nodes[cur.idx];
133        for(const Node &nb : here.neighboors())   // ADAPT: neighboors()
134        {
135            if(stats)
136                ++stats->generated;
137            const int ng = cur.g + nb.distToPrevious();   // ADAPT: distToPrevious()
138            const size_t found = index.find(nodes, nb);
139            if(found == npos)
140            {
141                nodes.push_back(nb);
142                parent.push_back(cur.idx);
143                gCost.push_back(ng);
144                hCost.push_back(nb.h(goal));   // ADAPT: h(goal)
145                closed.push_back(0);
146                index.add(nb, nodes.size() - 1);
147                open.push(OpenEntry{ng + hCost.back(), ng, nodes.size() - 1});
148            }
149            else if(ng < gCost[found])        // shorter way to a known node
150            {
151                gCost[found] = ng;
152                parent[found] = cur.idx;
153                closed[found] = 0;            // re-open (needed if h is inconsistent)
154                open.push(OpenEntry{ng + hCost[found], ng, found});
155            }
156        }
157    }
158    return {};
159}
160
161} // namespace astar_snip

166template<class Node>
167std::vector<Node> astar(const Node &start, const Node &goal,
168                        astar_snip::Stats *stats = nullptr)
169{
170    astar_snip::LinearIndex<Node> index;
171    return astar_snip::core(start, goal, index, stats);
172}

174// Same, with a key function for fast duplicate detection.
175// ADAPT: key must be identical for equal states, e.g. [](const Puzzle &p){ return p.str(); }
176template<class Node, class KeyFn>
177std::vector<Node> astarKeyed(const Node &start, const Node &goal, KeyFn key,
178                             astar_snip::Stats *stats = nullptr)

184// Demo node: 8-puzzle (3x3 sliding tiles). 0 is the blank.
185// ADAPT: replace this whole struct by your own state (keep the 4 interface methods).
186struct Puzzle
187{
188    std::array<int, 9> t;
189
190    explicit Puzzle(const std::array<int, 9> &tiles) : t(tiles) {}
191
192    bool operator==(const Puzzle &o) const { return t == o.t; }
193
194    int distToPrevious() const { return 1; }
195
196    // Manhattan distance of every tile (blank excluded) to its place in 'goal'.
197    double h(const Puzzle &goal) const
198    {
199        int total = 0;
200        for(int i = 0; i < 9; ++i)
201        {
202            if(t[static_cast<size_t>(i)] == 0)
203                continue;
204            int gi = 0;
205            for(int j = 0; j < 9; ++j)
206                if(goal.t[static_cast<size_t>(j)] == t[static_cast<size_t>(i)])
207                    gi = j;
208            total += std::abs(i / 3 - gi / 3) + std::abs(i % 3 - gi % 3);
209        }
210        return static_cast<double>(total);
211    }
212
213    std::vector<Puzzle> neighboors() const
214    {
215        std::vector<Puzzle> res;
216        int z = 0;
217        for(int i = 0; i < 9; ++i)
218            if(t[static_cast<size_t>(i)] == 0)
219                z = i;
220        const int r = z / 3, c = z % 3;
221        const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
222        const int dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
223        for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
224        {
225            const int nr = r + dr[k], nc = c + dc[k];
226            if(nr < 0 || nr > 2 || nc < 0 || nc > 2)
227                continue;
228            Puzzle n(*this);
229            std::swap(n.t[static_cast<size_t>(z)], n.t[static_cast<size_t>(nr * 3 + nc)]);
230            res.push_back(n);
231        }
232        return res;
233    }
234
235    // Move the blank in direction k (0 up, 1 down, 2 left, 3 right) if legal.
236    void slide(int k)
237    {
238        int z = 0;
239        for(int i = 0; i < 9; ++i)
240            if(t[static_cast<size_t>(i)] == 0)
241                z = i;
242        const int dr[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
243        const int dc[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
244        const int nr = z / 3 + dr[k], nc = z % 3 + dc[k];
245        if(nr < 0 || nr > 2 || nc < 0 || nc > 2)
246            return;
247        std::swap(t[static_cast<size_t>(z)], t[static_cast<size_t>(nr * 3 + nc)]);
248    }
249
250    std::string str() const
251    {
252        std::string s;
253        for(int i = 0; i < 9; ++i)
254        {
255            s += static_cast<char>('0' + t[static_cast<size_t>(i)]);
256            if(i % 3 == 2 && i != 8)
257                s += '/';
258        }
259        return s;
260    }
261
262    // Number of inversions (pairs out of order, blank ignored).
263    int inversions() const
264    {
265        int inv = 0;
266        for(int i = 0; i < 9; ++i)
267            for(int j = i + 1; j < 9; ++j)
268            {
269                const int a = t[static_cast<size_t>(i)], b = t[static_cast<size_t>(j)];
270                if(a != 0 && b != 0 && a > b)
271                    ++inv;
272            }
273        return inv;
274    }
275};
276
277// Solvability on an odd-width board: start can reach goal iff the inversion parities match.
278// 15-puzzle (width 4, even): solvable iff (inversions + row of the blank counted from the
279// bottom, 1-based) has the same parity as for the goal. Only this formula changes.
280bool solvable(const Puzzle &start, const Puzzle &goal)
281{
282    return (start.inversions() % 2) == (goal.inversions() % 2);
283}
284
285size_t moves(const std::vector<Puzzle> &path)
286{
287    return path.empty() ? size_t(0) : path.size() - 1;
288}

290// Plugging a Node into the course's own ecn::Astar  (maze/include/a_star.h)
291// Call:   std::vector<Node> path = ecn::Astar(start, goal);   // namespace ecn, header <a_star.h>
292// It prints stats ("nodes created, evaluated, shortcuts") and the time, returns the path.
293//
294// Requirements on Node, as actually used by a_star.h (differences with the interface above):
295//   * copy/move constructible (the tree stores copies in a std::vector<Node>)
296//   * bool operator==(const Node&) const
297//   * int distToPrevious() const
298//   * std::vector<Node> neighboors() const
299//   * int h(const Node &goal) const          <-- returns INT here (it is stored as int)
300//   * void print(const Node &next) const     <-- REQUIRED: fullPathTo() calls
301//                                                 path[i-1].print(path[i]) for each step
302// ecn::Astar does not need a key function (it searches its queue linearly: slow on big
303// state spaces, fine for mazes). Compile with the course header on the include path:
304//   g++ -std=c++17 -DUSE_ECN_ASTAR -I<course>/maze/include astar.cpp
305// The wrapper below is compiled only with -DUSE_ECN_ASTAR, so this file still builds alone.
306#ifdef USE_ECN_ASTAR
307#include <a_star.h>
308
309struct EcnPuzzle
310{
311    Puzzle p;
312    explicit EcnPuzzle(const Puzzle &q) : p(q) {}
313    bool operator==(const EcnPuzzle &o) const { return p == o.p; }
314    int distToPrevious() const { return 1; }
315    int h(const EcnPuzzle &goal) const { return static_cast<int>(p.h(goal.p)); }
316    std::vector<EcnPuzzle> neighboors() const
317    {
318        std::vector<EcnPuzzle> res;
319        for(const Puzzle &n : p.neighboors())
320            res.push_back(EcnPuzzle(n));
321        return res;
322    }
323    void print(const EcnPuzzle &next) const
324    {
325        std::cout << p.str() << " -> " << next.p.str() << "\n";
326    }
327};
328
329void ecnDemo(const Puzzle &start, const Puzzle &goal)
330{
331    ecn::Astar(EcnPuzzle(start), EcnPuzzle(goal));
332}
333#endif
334
335int main()
336{
337    const Puzzle goal(std::array<int, 9>{{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 0}});
338
339    // Build a start by sliding the blank around from the goal (always solvable).
340    Puzzle start = goal;
341    const int scramble[] = {1, 3, 3, 0, 2, 1, 3, 0, 0, 2, 2, 1, 1, 3, 3, 0, 2, 1, 3, 0, 2, 1};
342    for(int k : scramble)
343        start.slide(k);
344    std::cout << "start " << start.str() << "  goal " << goal.str() << "\n";
345    std::cout << "solvable: " << (solvable(start, goal) ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";
346
347    astar_snip::Stats st;
348    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
349    const std::vector<Puzzle> path = astarKeyed(start, goal,
350        [](const Puzzle &p) { return p.str(); }, &st);   // ADAPT: key function
351    const auto ms = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(
352                        std::chrono::steady_clock::now() - t0).count();
353    std::cout << "solution in " << moves(path) << " moves, "
354              << st.expanded << " expanded, " << st.generated << " generated, "
355              << ms << " ms\n";
356    for(size_t i = 0; i < path.size(); ++i)
357        std::cout << "  " << i << ": " << path[i].str() << "\n";
358
359    // The same with the linear-lookup version (only needs ==), fine for small searches.
360    const std::vector<Puzzle> path2 = astar(start, goal);
361    std::cout << "linear version gives " << moves(path2) << " moves (must be equal)\n";
362
363    // An unsolvable board: swap two tiles of the goal.
364    const Puzzle bad(std::array<int, 9>{{2, 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 0}});
365    std::cout << bad.str() << " solvable: " << (solvable(bad, goal) ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";
366
367#ifdef USE_ECN_ASTAR
368    ecnDemo(start, goal);
369#endif
370    return 0;
371}

  1// bfs_dfs.cpp - BFS shortest path, recursive + iterative DFS, flood fill on a char grid.
  2// Build: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 bfs_dfs.cpp -o bfs_dfs
  3//
  4// Grid convention used here: vector<string>, '#' = wall, ' ' or '.' = free,
  5// 'S' = start, 'G' = goal. Cell = (row, col).
  6// ADAPT: isFree() decides what is walkable; DR/DC list the allowed moves
  7// (4 neighbours here; add the 4 diagonals for 8-connectivity).
  8#include <algorithm>
  9#include <iostream>
 10#include <queue>
 11#include <stack>
 12#include <string>
 13#include <utility>
 14#include <vector>
 15
 16using Grid = std::vector<std::string>;
 17using Cell = std::pair<int, int>;   // (row, col)
 18
 19const int DR[4] = {-1, 1, 0, 0};
 20const int DC[4] = {0, 0, -1, 1};
 21
 22bool inside(const Grid &g, int r, int c)
 23{
 24    return r >= 0 && r < static_cast<int>(g.size())
 25        && c >= 0 && c < static_cast<int>(g[static_cast<size_t>(r)].size());
 26}
 27
 28// ADAPT: what can we walk on?
 29bool isFree(const Grid &g, int r, int c)
 30{
 31    return inside(g, r, c) && g[static_cast<size_t>(r)][static_cast<size_t>(c)] != '#';
 32}
 33
 34Cell findChar(const Grid &g, char ch)
 35{
 36    for(size_t r = 0; r < g.size(); ++r)
 37        for(size_t c = 0; c < g[r].size(); ++c)
 38            if(g[r][c] == ch)
 39                return Cell(static_cast<int>(r), static_cast<int>(c));
 40    return Cell(-1, -1);
 41}
 42
 43// BFS: shortest path (fewest steps) on an unweighted grid.
 44// Returns the path start..goal, empty if unreachable.
 45std::vector<Cell> bfs(const Grid &g, Cell start, Cell goal)
 46{
 47    const size_t rows = g.size();
 48    const size_t cols = g.empty() ? 0 : g[0].size();
 49    // parent[r][c] = cell we came from; (-1,-1) = not visited yet
 50    std::vector<std::vector<Cell>> parent(rows, std::vector<Cell>(cols, Cell(-1, -1)));
 51    std::queue<Cell> q;
 52    q.push(start);
 53    parent[static_cast<size_t>(start.first)][static_cast<size_t>(start.second)] = start;
 54
 55    while(!q.empty())
 56    {
 57        const Cell cur = q.front();
 58        q.pop();
 59        if(cur == goal)
 60        {
 61            std::vector<Cell> path;
 62            for(Cell p = goal; p != start;
 63                p = parent[static_cast<size_t>(p.first)][static_cast<size_t>(p.second)])
 64                path.push_back(p);
 65            path.push_back(start);
 66            std::reverse(path.begin(), path.end());
 67            return path;
 68        }
 69        for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
 70        {
 71            const int nr = cur.first + DR[k], nc = cur.second + DC[k];
 72            if(!isFree(g, nr, nc))
 73                continue;
 74            Cell &par = parent[static_cast<size_t>(nr)][static_cast<size_t>(nc)];
 75            if(par.first != -1)          // already visited
 76                continue;
 77            par = cur;
 78            q.push(Cell(nr, nc));
 79        }
 80    }
 81    return {};
 82}
 83
 84// BFS distance map (-1 = unreachable).
 85std::vector<std::vector<int>> bfsDistances(const Grid &g, Cell start)
 86{
 87    const size_t rows = g.size();
 88    const size_t cols = g.empty() ? 0 : g[0].size();
 89    std::vector<std::vector<int>> dist(rows, std::vector<int>(cols, -1));
 90    std::queue<Cell> q;
 91    q.push(start);
 92    dist[static_cast<size_t>(start.first)][static_cast<size_t>(start.second)] = 0;
 93    while(!q.empty())
 94    {
 95        const Cell cur = q.front();
 96        q.pop();
 97        const int d = dist[static_cast<size_t>(cur.first)][static_cast<size_t>(cur.second)];
 98        for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
 99        {
100            const int nr = cur.first + DR[k], nc = cur.second + DC[k];
101            if(!isFree(g, nr, nc) ||
102               dist[static_cast<size_t>(nr)][static_cast<size_t>(nc)] != -1)
103                continue;
104            dist[static_cast<size_t>(nr)][static_cast<size_t>(nc)] = d + 1;
105            q.push(Cell(nr, nc));
106        }
107    }
108    return dist;
109}
110
111// Recursive DFS: finds A path (not the shortest). 'path' is built with push/pop = backtracking.
112bool dfsRec(const Grid &g, Cell cur, Cell goal,
113            std::vector<std::vector<char>> &seen, std::vector<Cell> &path)
114{
115    seen[static_cast<size_t>(cur.first)][static_cast<size_t>(cur.second)] = 1;
116    path.push_back(cur);
117    if(cur == goal)
118        return true;
119    for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
120    {
121        const int nr = cur.first + DR[k], nc = cur.second + DC[k];
122        if(!isFree(g, nr, nc) || seen[static_cast<size_t>(nr)][static_cast<size_t>(nc)])
123            continue;
124        if(dfsRec(g, Cell(nr, nc), goal, seen, path))
125            return true;
126    }
127    path.pop_back();     // dead end: undo
128    return false;
129}
130
131std::vector<Cell> dfsRecursive(const Grid &g, Cell start, Cell goal)
132{
133    std::vector<std::vector<char>> seen(g.size(), std::vector<char>(g[0].size(), 0));
134    std::vector<Cell> path;
135    if(!dfsRec(g, start, goal, seen, path))
136        path.clear();
137    return path;
138}
139
140// Iterative DFS with an explicit stack (no recursion depth limit). Returns visit order.
141// To rebuild a path, store parent[] exactly like in bfs().
142std::vector<Cell> dfsIterativeOrder(const Grid &g, Cell start)
143{
144    std::vector<std::vector<char>> seen(g.size(), std::vector<char>(g[0].size(), 0));
145    std::vector<Cell> order;
146    std::stack<Cell> st;
147    st.push(start);
148    while(!st.empty())
149    {
150        const Cell cur = st.top();
151        st.pop();
152        char &s = seen[static_cast<size_t>(cur.first)][static_cast<size_t>(cur.second)];
153        if(s)
154            continue;
155        s = 1;
156        order.push_back(cur);
157        for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
158        {
159            const int nr = cur.first + DR[k], nc = cur.second + DC[k];
160            if(isFree(g, nr, nc) && !seen[static_cast<size_t>(nr)][static_cast<size_t>(nc)])
161                st.push(Cell(nr, nc));
162        }
163    }
164    return order;
165}
166
167// Flood fill (modifies the grid): replace the connected region around (r,c) by 'fill'.
168// Returns the number of cells changed.
169// ADAPT: 'target' is the character being replaced (read from the start cell).
170int floodFill(Grid &g, int r, int c, char fill)
171{
172    if(!inside(g, r, c))
173        return 0;
174    const char target = g[static_cast<size_t>(r)][static_cast<size_t>(c)];
175    if(target == fill)
176        return 0;
177    int count = 0;
178    std::stack<Cell> st;
179    st.push(Cell(r, c));
180    while(!st.empty())
181    {
182        const Cell cur = st.top();
183        st.pop();
184        if(!inside(g, cur.first, cur.second))
185            continue;
186        char &ch = g[static_cast<size_t>(cur.first)][static_cast<size_t>(cur.second)];
187        if(ch != target)
188            continue;
189        ch = fill;
190        ++count;
191        for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
192            st.push(Cell(cur.first + DR[k], cur.second + DC[k]));
193    }
194    return count;
195}
196
197// Count connected free regions (components) using floodFill on a copy.
198int countRegions(Grid g)
199{
200    int regions = 0;
201    // normalise: every non-wall char ('S', 'G', ...) becomes '.', so one region = one colour
202    for(std::string &row : g)
203        for(char &ch : row)
204            if(ch != '#')
205                ch = '.';
206    for(size_t r = 0; r < g.size(); ++r)
207        for(size_t c = 0; c < g[r].size(); ++c)
208            if(g[r][c] != '#' && g[r][c] != '~')
209            {
210                floodFill(g, static_cast<int>(r), static_cast<int>(c), '~');
211                ++regions;
212            }
213    return regions;
214}
215
216void printGrid(const Grid &g)
217{
218    for(const std::string &row : g)
219        std::cout << row << "\n";
220}
221
222int main()
223{
224    Grid maze = {
225        "S...#.......",
226        ".##.#.#####.",
227        ".#..#.#...#.",
228        ".#.##.#.#.#.",
229        ".#....#.#...",
230        ".######.###.",
231        "........#..G",
232    };
233    const Cell start = findChar(maze, 'S');
234    const Cell goal = findChar(maze, 'G');
235
236    const std::vector<Cell> sp = bfs(maze, start, goal);
237    std::cout << "BFS shortest path: " << (sp.empty() ? 0 : sp.size() - 1) << " steps\n";
238    Grid shown = maze;
239    for(const Cell &c : sp)
240        if(shown[static_cast<size_t>(c.first)][static_cast<size_t>(c.second)] == '.')
241            shown[static_cast<size_t>(c.first)][static_cast<size_t>(c.second)] = '*';
242    printGrid(shown);
243
244    const auto dist = bfsDistances(maze, start);
245    std::cout << "distance map says goal is at "
246              << dist[static_cast<size_t>(goal.first)][static_cast<size_t>(goal.second)] << "\n";
247
248    const std::vector<Cell> dp = dfsRecursive(maze, start, goal);
249    std::cout << "DFS (recursive) found a path of " << (dp.empty() ? 0 : dp.size() - 1)
250              << " steps (not necessarily shortest)\n";
251
252    const std::vector<Cell> order = dfsIterativeOrder(maze, start);
253    std::cout << "iterative DFS visited " << order.size() << " cells\n";
254
255    std::cout << "free regions before: " << countRegions(maze) << "\n";
256    Grid filled = maze;
257    const int n = floodFill(filled, 0, 1, 'o');
258    std::cout << "flood fill from (0,1) changed " << n << " cells:\n";
259    printGrid(filled);
260
261    Grid split = {
262        "..#..",
263        "..#..",
264        "###..",
265    };
266    std::cout << "regions in the split grid: " << countRegions(split) << "\n";
267    return 0;
268}

  1// minimax_alphabeta.cpp - negamax + alpha-beta (and plain minimax) on a generic game
  2// interface. Demos: Nim sticks and Connect Four 6x7.
  3// Build: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 minimax_alphabeta.cpp -o minimax_alphabeta
  4//
  5// Game interface (what YOUR game class must provide; ADAPT everything below it):
  6//     using Move = int;                          // any copyable type
  7//     std::vector<Move> validMoves() const;      // legal moves for the player to move
  8//     void play(const Move &m);                  // apply move, switch player
  9//     void undo(const Move &m);                  // exact inverse of play(m), switch back
 10//     bool isTerminal() const;                   // game over (win/loss/draw)?
 11//     int  evaluate() const;                     // score FROM THE POINT OF VIEW OF THE
 12//                                                // PLAYER TO MOVE: >0 good for him.
 13//                                                // Lost position (previous mover just won)
 14//                                                // must return -WIN. Draw -> 0.
 15//
 16// Negamax trick: score(player) = -score(opponent), so ONE function replaces the
 17// separate max and min functions of textbook minimax:
 18//     value = -negamax(child, depth-1, -beta, -alpha)
 19// alpha = best score the player to move is already sure of,
 20// beta  = best score the opponent would allow. If alpha >= beta -> prune (break).
 21#include <algorithm>
 22#include <iostream>
 23#include <string>
 24#include <vector>
 25
 26const int WIN = 100000;   // score of a won position (heuristics must stay far below)
 27
 28template<class Move>
 29struct SearchResult
 30{
 31    Move move{};
 32    int score = 0;
 33    long nodes = 0;
 34};
 35
 36// Plain negamax, no pruning (reference version).
 37template<class G>
 38int negamaxPlain(G &g, int depth, long &nodes)
 39{
 40    ++nodes;
 41    if(g.isTerminal() || depth == 0)
 42    {
 43        int s = g.evaluate();
 44        if(s >= WIN) s += depth;            // prefer quicker wins...
 45        else if(s <= -WIN) s -= depth;      // ...and slower losses
 46        return s;
 47    }
 48    int best = -2 * WIN;
 49    for(const auto &m : g.validMoves())
 50    {
 51        g.play(m);
 52        best = std::max(best, -negamaxPlain(g, depth - 1, nodes));
 53        g.undo(m);
 54    }
 55    return best;
 56}
 57
 58// Negamax with alpha-beta pruning and a depth limit. Call with
 59// alpha = -2*WIN, beta = 2*WIN at the root.
 60template<class G>
 61int negamax(G &g, int depth, int alpha, int beta, long &nodes)
 62{
 63    ++nodes;
 64    if(g.isTerminal() || depth == 0)
 65    {
 66        int s = g.evaluate();               // ADAPT: heuristic at depth limit
 67        if(s >= WIN) s += depth;
 68        else if(s <= -WIN) s -= depth;
 69        return s;
 70    }
 71    int best = -2 * WIN;
 72    for(const auto &m : g.validMoves())     // ADAPT: move ORDERING matters a lot
 73    {
 74        g.play(m);
 75        const int v = -negamax(g, depth - 1, -beta, -alpha, nodes);
 76        g.undo(m);
 77        if(v > best)
 78            best = v;
 79        if(best > alpha)
 80            alpha = best;
 81        if(alpha >= beta)
 82            break;                          // cut-off: opponent will never allow this line
 83    }
 84    return best;
 85}
 86
 87// Root: best move with its score and node count.
 88template<class G>
 89SearchResult<typename G::Move> bestMove(G &g, int depth, bool prune = true)
 90{
 91    SearchResult<typename G::Move> res;
 92    int alpha = -2 * WIN;
 93    const int beta = 2 * WIN;
 94    int best = -4 * WIN;
 95    for(const auto &m : g.validMoves())
 96    {
 97        g.play(m);
 98        const int v = prune ? -negamax(g, depth - 1, -beta, -alpha, res.nodes)
 99                            : -negamaxPlain(g, depth - 1, res.nodes);
100        g.undo(m);
101        if(v > best)
102        {
103            best = v;
104            res.move = m;
105        }
106        if(best > alpha)
107            alpha = best;
108    }
109    res.score = best;
110    return res;
111}
112

127// Game 1: Nim with sticks. Take 1..3 sticks, whoever takes the LAST stick wins.
128// (Variant "last stick loses": change evaluate() to +WIN when sticks == 0, since then
129//  the player to move has WON because the opponent took the last one.)
130class Nim
131{
132public:
133    using Move = int;
134    explicit Nim(int sticks) : sticks_(sticks) {}
135
136    std::vector<int> validMoves() const
137    {
138        std::vector<int> m;
139        for(int k = 1; k <= 3 && k <= sticks_; ++k)   // ADAPT: max take
140            m.push_back(k);
141        return m;
142    }
143    void play(const int &k) { sticks_ -= k; }
144    void undo(const int &k) { sticks_ += k; }
145    bool isTerminal() const { return sticks_ == 0; }
146    int evaluate() const { return sticks_ == 0 ? -WIN : 0; }  // mover facing 0 sticks lost
147    int sticks() const { return sticks_; }
148
149private:
150    int sticks_;
151};
152
153// Game 2: Connect Four, 6 rows x 7 columns. Players are +1 (first) and -1 (second).
154// Move = column index 0..6.
155class Connect4
156{
157public:
158    using Move = int;
159    static constexpr int ROWS = 6;
160    static constexpr int COLS = 7;
161
162    Connect4() : turn_(1)
163    {
164        for(int r = 0; r < ROWS; ++r)
165            for(int c = 0; c < COLS; ++c)
166                b_[r][c] = 0;
167        for(int c = 0; c < COLS; ++c)
168            h_[c] = 0;
169    }
170
171    // Centre columns first: good ordering = many more cut-offs.
172    std::vector<int> validMoves() const
173    {
174        static const int order[COLS] = {3, 2, 4, 1, 5, 0, 6};
175        std::vector<int> m;
176        for(int k = 0; k < COLS; ++k)
177            if(h_[order[k]] < ROWS)
178                m.push_back(order[k]);
179        return m;
180    }
181
182    void play(const int &c)
183    {
184        b_[h_[c]][c] = turn_;
185        ++h_[c];
186        hist_.push_back(c);
187        turn_ = -turn_;
188    }
189
190    void undo(const int &c)
191    {
192        --h_[c];
193        b_[h_[c]][c] = 0;
194        hist_.pop_back();
195        turn_ = -turn_;
196    }
197
198    // Did the disc that was just played complete four in a row?
199    bool lastMoveWon() const
200    {
201        if(hist_.empty())
202            return false;
203        const int c = hist_.back();
204        const int r = h_[c] - 1;
205        const int p = b_[r][c];
206        static const int dir[4][2] = {{0, 1}, {1, 0}, {1, 1}, {1, -1}};
207        for(int d = 0; d < 4; ++d)
208        {
209            int n = 1;
210            for(int sign = -1; sign <= 1; sign += 2)
211                for(int k = 1; k < 4; ++k)
212                {
213                    const int rr = r + sign * dir[d][0] * k;
214                    const int cc = c + sign * dir[d][1] * k;
215                    if(rr < 0 || rr >= ROWS || cc < 0 || cc >= COLS || b_[rr][cc] != p)
216                        break;
217                    ++n;
218                }
219            if(n >= 4)
220                return true;
221        }
222        return false;
223    }
224
225    bool full() const { return hist_.size() == static_cast<size_t>(ROWS * COLS); }
226    bool isTerminal() const { return lastMoveWon() || full(); }
227
228    // Score for the player TO MOVE.
229    int evaluate() const
230    {
231        if(lastMoveWon())
232            return -WIN;          // the previous mover just won
233        if(full())
234            return 0;
235        int score = 0;
236        // centre column is worth a bit
237        for(int r = 0; r < ROWS; ++r)
238            score += 3 * b_[r][COLS / 2] * turn_;
239        // every window of 4 cells
240        static const int dir[4][2] = {{0, 1}, {1, 0}, {1, 1}, {1, -1}};
241        for(int r = 0; r < ROWS; ++r)
242            for(int c = 0; c < COLS; ++c)
243                for(int d = 0; d < 4; ++d)
244                {
245                    const int er = r + 3 * dir[d][0], ec = c + 3 * dir[d][1];
246                    if(er < 0 || er >= ROWS || ec < 0 || ec >= COLS)
247                        continue;
248                    int mine = 0, theirs = 0;
249                    for(int k = 0; k < 4; ++k)
250                    {
251                        const int v = b_[r + k * dir[d][0]][c + k * dir[d][1]] * turn_;
252                        if(v > 0) ++mine;
253                        else if(v < 0) ++theirs;
254                    }
255                    if(mine > 0 && theirs > 0)
256                        continue;
257                    if(mine == 3) score += 50;
258                    else if(mine == 2) score += 10;
259                    else if(mine == 1) score += 1;
260                    if(theirs == 3) score -= 50;
261                    else if(theirs == 2) score -= 10;
262                    else if(theirs == 1) score -= 1;
263                }
264        return score;
265    }
266
267    void print() const
268    {
269        for(int r = ROWS - 1; r >= 0; --r)
270        {
271            for(int c = 0; c < COLS; ++c)
272                std::cout << (b_[r][c] > 0 ? 'X' : (b_[r][c] < 0 ? 'O' : '.')) << ' ';
273            std::cout << "\n";
274        }
275        std::cout << "0 1 2 3 4 5 6\n";
276    }
277
278    int turn() const { return turn_; }
279
280private:
281    int b_[ROWS][COLS];   // b_[0] = bottom row
282    int h_[COLS];         // number of discs in each column
283    int turn_;            // +1 or -1: who plays next
284    std::vector<int> hist_;
285};
286
287int main()
288{
289    // --- Nim: 21 sticks, the winning move is to leave a multiple of 4 -> take 1
290    {
291        Nim nim(21);
292        const auto r = bestMove(nim, 99);
293        std::cout << "Nim 21 sticks: best take = " << r.move << " (score " << r.score
294                  << ", alpha-beta nodes " << r.nodes << ")\n";
295        Nim nim2(21);
296        const auto r2 = bestMove(nim2, 99, false);
297        std::cout << "  same without pruning: best take = " << r2.move
298                  << ", nodes " << r2.nodes << "\n";
299    }
300
301    // --- Connect Four: tactical position, X has 3 in a row on the bottom and must win
302    {
303        Connect4 g;
304        const int opening[] = {3, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5};
305        for(int c : opening)
306            g.play(c);
307        g.print();
308        const auto r = bestMove(g, 4);
309        std::cout << "X to move, best column = " << r.move << " (score " << r.score
310                  << ", nodes " << r.nodes << ")  -> 2 or 6 wins at once\n";
311    }
312
313    // --- Connect Four: computer vs computer for a few moves (depth 6)
314    {
315        Connect4 g;
316        long totalNodes = 0;
317        for(int move = 0; move < 8 && !g.isTerminal(); ++move)
318        {
319            const auto r = bestMove(g, 6);
320            totalNodes += r.nodes;
321            std::cout << (g.turn() > 0 ? "X" : "O") << " plays column " << r.move
322                      << " (score " << r.score << ", nodes " << r.nodes << ")\n";
323            g.play(r.move);
324        }
325        g.print();
326        std::cout << "total nodes: " << totalNodes << "\n";
327    }
328    return 0;
329}
