  1// genetic_algorithm.cpp - genetic algorithm on permutations (TSP demo, 15 cities).
  2// Build: g++ -std=c++17 -Wall -Wextra -O2 genetic_algorithm.cpp -o genetic_algorithm
  3//
  4// GA loop (one generation):
  5//   1. evaluate cost (fitness) of every individual
  6//   2. elitism: copy the best few unchanged into the next generation
  7//   3. fill the rest: pick 2 parents by TOURNAMENT selection, CROSSOVER them (OX for
  8//      permutations), MUTATE the child with small probability, evaluate it
  9//   4. replace the population, repeat
 10// Here lower cost = better (tour length). For "maximise", flip the comparisons.
 11//
 12// ADAPT: Individual (the genome), cost(), randomIndividual(), crossover(), mutate().
 13// The loop in evolve() does not care what the genome is.
 14#include <algorithm>
 15#include <cmath>
 16#include <cstddef>
 17#include <iostream>
 18#include <numeric>
 19#include <random>
 20#include <vector>
 21
 22struct City
 23{
 24    double x, y;
 25};
 26
 27// Problem definition (ADAPT)
 28struct Individual
 29{
 30    std::vector<int> genes;    // a permutation of 0..n-1 = visiting order
 31    double cost = 0.0;         // tour length (lower is better)
 32};
 33
 34double tourLength(const std::vector<int> &tour, const std::vector<City> &cities)
 35{
 36    double total = 0.0;
 37    for(size_t i = 0; i < tour.size(); ++i)
 38    {
 39        const City &a = cities[static_cast<size_t>(tour[i])];
 40        const City &b = cities[static_cast<size_t>(tour[(i + 1) % tour.size()])];
 41        total += std::hypot(a.x - b.x, a.y - b.y);
 42    }
 43    return total;
 44}
 45
 46Individual randomIndividual(size_t n, std::mt19937 &rng)
 47{
 48    Individual ind;
 49    ind.genes.resize(n);
 50    std::iota(ind.genes.begin(), ind.genes.end(), 0);
 51    std::shuffle(ind.genes.begin(), ind.genes.end(), rng);
 52    return ind;
 53}
 54
 55// Order crossover (OX): copy a slice of parent 1, fill the rest in the ORDER in which
 56// the missing cities appear in parent 2 (starting after the slice, wrapping around).
 57// Always yields a valid permutation.
 58std::vector<int> orderCrossover(const std::vector<int> &p1, const std::vector<int> &p2,
 59                                std::mt19937 &rng)
 60{
 61    const size_t n = p1.size();
 62    std::uniform_int_distribution<size_t> pick(0, n - 1);
 63    size_t a = pick(rng), b = pick(rng);
 64    if(a > b)
 65        std::swap(a, b);
 66
 67    std::vector<int> child(n, -1);
 68    std::vector<char> used(n, 0);
 69    for(size_t i = a; i <= b; ++i)
 70    {
 71        child[i] = p1[i];
 72        used[static_cast<size_t>(p1[i])] = 1;
 73    }
 74    size_t pos = (b + 1) % n;
 75    for(size_t k = 0; k < n; ++k)
 76    {
 77        const int city = p2[(b + 1 + k) % n];
 78        if(used[static_cast<size_t>(city)])
 79            continue;
 80        child[pos] = city;
 81        used[static_cast<size_t>(city)] = 1;
 82        pos = (pos + 1) % n;
 83    }
 84    return child;
 85}
 86
 87// Mutation 1: swap two random positions.
 88void swapMutation(std::vector<int> &g, std::mt19937 &rng)
 89{
 90    std::uniform_int_distribution<size_t> pick(0, g.size() - 1);
 91    std::swap(g[pick(rng)], g[pick(rng)]);
 92}
 93
 94// Mutation 2: reverse a random slice (like a 2-opt move, usually better for TSP).
 95void inversionMutation(std::vector<int> &g, std::mt19937 &rng)
 96{
 97    std::uniform_int_distribution<size_t> pick(0, g.size() - 1);
 98    size_t a = pick(rng), b = pick(rng);
 99    if(a > b)
100        std::swap(a, b);
101    std::reverse(g.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(a),
102                 g.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(b) + 1);
103}
104
105// Generic GA machinery
106struct Params
107{
108    size_t populationSize = 150;
109    size_t generations = 300;
110    size_t elite = 2;              // best individuals copied unchanged
111    size_t tournamentSize = 4;     // bigger = more selection pressure
112    double crossoverRate = 0.9;
113    double mutationRate = 0.25;
114};
115
116// Tournament selection: draw k random individuals, return the best one.
117const Individual &tournament(const std::vector<Individual> &pop, size_t k, std::mt19937 &rng)
118{
119    std::uniform_int_distribution<size_t> pick(0, pop.size() - 1);
120    const Individual *best = &pop[pick(rng)];
121    for(size_t i = 1; i < k; ++i)
122    {
123        const Individual *cand = &pop[pick(rng)];
124        if(cand->cost < best->cost)
125            best = cand;
126    }
127    return *best;
128}
129
130bool isPermutation(const std::vector<int> &g)
131{
132    std::vector<int> sorted(g);
133    std::sort(sorted.begin(), sorted.end());
134    for(size_t i = 0; i < sorted.size(); ++i)
135        if(sorted[i] != static_cast<int>(i))
136            return false;
137    return true;
138}
139
140Individual evolve(const std::vector<City> &cities, const Params &prm, std::mt19937 &rng,
141                  bool verbose)
142{
143    const size_t n = cities.size();
144    std::uniform_real_distribution<double> unit(0.0, 1.0);
145    auto byCost = [](const Individual &a, const Individual &b) { return a.cost < b.cost; };
146
147    std::vector<Individual> pop;
148    for(size_t i = 0; i < prm.populationSize; ++i)
149    {
150        pop.push_back(randomIndividual(n, rng));
151        pop.back().cost = tourLength(pop.back().genes, cities);    // ADAPT: cost()
152    }
153
154    for(size_t gen = 0; gen <= prm.generations; ++gen)
155    {
156        std::sort(pop.begin(), pop.end(), byCost);       // best first
157        if(verbose && gen % 50 == 0)
158            std::cout << "gen " << gen << "  best " << pop.front().cost << "\n";
159        if(gen == prm.generations)
160            break;
161
162        std::vector<Individual> next(pop.begin(), pop.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(prm.elite));
163        while(next.size() < prm.populationSize)
164        {
165            const Individual &p1 = tournament(pop, prm.tournamentSize, rng);
166            const Individual &p2 = tournament(pop, prm.tournamentSize, rng);
167            Individual child;
168            child.genes = (unit(rng) < prm.crossoverRate)
169                              ? orderCrossover(p1.genes, p2.genes, rng)   // ADAPT: crossover
170                              : p1.genes;
171            if(unit(rng) < prm.mutationRate)
172            {
173                if(unit(rng) < 0.5)
174                    swapMutation(child.genes, rng);                       // ADAPT: mutation
175                else
176                    inversionMutation(child.genes, rng);
177            }
178            child.cost = tourLength(child.genes, cities);
179            next.push_back(child);
180        }
181        pop.swap(next);
182    }
183    return pop.front();
184}
185
186int main()
187{
188    std::mt19937 rng(12345);   // fixed seed -> reproducible run
189    std::uniform_real_distribution<double> coord(0.0, 100.0);
190
191    std::vector<City> cities;
192    for(int i = 0; i < 15; ++i)
193    {
194        City c;
195        c.x = coord(rng);
196        c.y = coord(rng);
197        cities.push_back(c);
198    }
199
200    // Baseline: nearest-neighbour greedy tour from city 0
201    std::vector<int> greedy{0};
202    std::vector<char> seen(cities.size(), 0);
203    seen[0] = 1;
204    while(greedy.size() < cities.size())
205    {
206        const City &last = cities[static_cast<size_t>(greedy.back())];
207        int bestCity = -1;
208        double bestD = 1e18;
209        for(size_t c = 0; c < cities.size(); ++c)
210        {
211            if(seen[c])
212                continue;
213            const double d = std::hypot(last.x - cities[c].x, last.y - cities[c].y);
214            if(d < bestD)
215            {
216                bestD = d;
217                bestCity = static_cast<int>(c);
218            }
219        }
220        seen[static_cast<size_t>(bestCity)] = 1;
221        greedy.push_back(bestCity);
222    }
223    std::cout << "nearest-neighbour baseline: " << tourLength(greedy, cities) << "\n";
224
225    Params prm;
226    const Individual best = evolve(cities, prm, rng, true);
227    std::cout << "GA best length: " << best.cost << "\n";
228    std::cout << "tour:";
229    for(int c : best.genes)
230        std::cout << ' ' << c;
231    std::cout << "\nvalid permutation: " << (isPermutation(best.genes) ? "yes" : "NO") << "\n";
232    return 0;
233}

 33// 1. priority_queue is a MAX-heap: top() = largest according to "less".
 34//    For a MIN-heap the comparator must say "a is worse than b" when a > b.
 35// 1a. integers: std::greater
 36using MinHeapInt = std::priority_queue<int, std::vector<int>, std::greater<int>>;
 37
 38// 1b. comparator struct (reusable, e.g. for A* open set). ADAPT: the member compared.
 39struct TaskWorse
 40{
 41    bool operator()(const Task &a, const Task &b) const { return a.cost > b.cost; }
 42};
 43using TaskQueue = std::priority_queue<Task, std::vector<Task>, TaskWorse>;

 45// 1c. pair<f, id> works out of the box with std::greater (compares first, then second)
 46using FQueue = std::priority_queue<std::pair<double, int>,
 47                                   std::vector<std::pair<double, int>>,
 48                                   std::greater<std::pair<double, int>>>;

 83// 2. Custom keys
 84// 2a. std::map works with pair<int,int> directly (pair has operator<). O(log n).
 85// 2b. unordered_map needs a hash. Hash for pair<int,int>:
 86struct PairHash
 87{
 88    size_t operator()(const std::pair<int, int> &p) const
 89    {
 90        const unsigned long long a = static_cast<unsigned int>(p.first);
 91        const unsigned long long b = static_cast<unsigned int>(p.second);
 92        return std::hash<unsigned long long>()((a << 32) | b);
 93    }
 94};
 95
 96// 2c. a struct as key: needs operator== (unordered) or operator< (ordered) + hash.
 97struct Pos
 98{
 99    int x, y;
100    bool operator==(const Pos &o) const { return x == o.x && y == o.y; }
101    bool operator<(const Pos &o) const { return std::tie(x, y) < std::tie(o.x, o.y); }
102};
103struct PosHash
104{
105    size_t operator()(const Pos &p) const
106    {
107        // classic hash combine
108        size_t h = std::hash<int>()(p.x);
109        h ^= std::hash<int>()(p.y) + 0x9e3779b9u + (h << 6) + (h >> 2);
110        return h;
111    }
112};

163// 4. erase-remove idiom. remove_if only MOVES the kept items to the front and
164//    returns the new end; erase then shrinks the vector.
165void demoEraseRemove()
166{
167    std::vector<int> v{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8};
168    v.erase(std::remove_if(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x % 2 == 0; }), v.end());
169    std::cout << "odd only:";
170    for(int x : v)
171        std::cout << ' ' << x;
172    std::cout << "\n";
173
174    std::vector<int> w{3, 1, 3, 2, 3};
175    w.erase(std::remove(w.begin(), w.end(), 3), w.end());
176    std::cout << "without 3s: " << w.size() << " items\n";
177
178    std::vector<int> d{1, 1, 2, 2, 2, 3, 1};
179    std::sort(d.begin(), d.end());
180    d.erase(std::unique(d.begin(), d.end()), d.end());          // dedupe (needs sorted)
181    std::cout << "unique sorted: " << d.size() << " items\n";
182
183    // Removing while iterating by index: remember to NOT increment after erase.
184    std::vector<int> e{1, 2, 2, 3};
185    for(size_t i = 0; i < e.size();)
186    {
187        if(e[i] == 2)
188            e.erase(e.begin() + static_cast<std::ptrdiff_t>(i));
189        else
190            ++i;
191    }
192    std::cout << "manual erase left " << e.size() << " items\n";
193}

223// 6. min_element with a comparator. Returns an ITERATOR (end() if empty!).
224//    comparator(a, b) == "a is smaller than b". Sudoku: pick cell with fewest candidates.
225struct Cell
226{
227    int id;
228    std::vector<int> candidates;
229};
230
231void demoMinElement()
232{
233    std::vector<Cell> cells{{0, {1, 2, 3}}, {1, {4}}, {2, {5, 6}}};
234    auto it = std::min_element(cells.begin(), cells.end(),
235        [](const Cell &a, const Cell &b) { return a.candidates.size() < b.candidates.size(); });
236    if(it != cells.end())
237        std::cout << "most constrained cell: " << it->id << " ("
238                  << it->candidates.size() << " candidate)\n";
239
240    // among pointers (typical when the grid owns the cells)
241    std::vector<Cell *> ptrs;
242    for(Cell &c : cells)
243        ptrs.push_back(&c);
244    auto itp = std::max_element(ptrs.begin(), ptrs.end(),
245        [](const Cell *a, const Cell *b) { return a->candidates.size() < b->candidates.size(); });
246    std::cout << "least constrained cell: " << (*itp)->id << "\n";
247
248    // skip already-decided cells: filter FIRST (copy the undecided ones) then min_element
249    std::vector<Cell *> todo;
250    for(Cell *c : ptrs)
251        if(c->candidates.size() > 1)
252            todo.push_back(c);
253    std::cout << "undecided cells: " << todo.size() << "\n";
254}

265    auto lb = std::lower_bound(v.begin(), v.end(), 16);     // sorted input only

267    std::cout << "any/all/none: " << std::any_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x == 8; })
268              << std::all_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x > 0; })
269              << std::none_of(v.begin(), v.end(), [](int x) { return x > 100; }) << "\n";
270    std::reverse(v.begin(), v.end());
271    std::rotate(v.begin(), v.begin() + 1, v.end());         // left-rotate by 1
272    std::cout << "after reverse+rotate front = " << v.front() << "\n";

  6//   * never use rand() % n (biased, low quality): use a distribution
  7//   * fixed seed  -> reproducible runs (debugging, GA comparisons)

  9#include <algorithm>

 18// Pick a random element of a non-empty vector (returns a reference).
 19// ADAPT: the container type.
 20template<class T>
 21const T &pickRandom(const std::vector<T> &v, std::mt19937 &rng)
 22{
 23    std::uniform_int_distribution<size_t> d(0, v.size() - 1);   // bounds are INCLUSIVE
 24    return v[d(rng)];
 25}
 26
 27// Time any callable, returns elapsed milliseconds as double.
 28template<class F>
 29double timeMs(F &&f)
 30{
 31    const auto t0 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
 32    f();
 33    const auto t1 = std::chrono::steady_clock::now();
 34    return std::chrono::duration<double, std::milli>(t1 - t0).count();
 35}

 37long long heavySum(int n)
 38{
 39    long long s = 0;
 40    for(int i = 0; i < n; ++i)
 41        s += (static_cast<long long>(i) * i) % 7;
 42    return s;
 43}

 11// Towers of Hanoi: move n discs from 'from' to 'to' using 'via'.
 12// Move n-1 to via, move the big one, move n-1 from via onto it. 2^n - 1 moves.
 13void hanoi(int n, char from, char to, char via, long long &moves, bool print)
 14{
 15    if(n == 0)
 16        return;
 17    hanoi(n - 1, from, via, to, moves, print);
 18    ++moves;
 19    if(print)
 20        std::cout << "  move disc " << n << " " << from << " -> " << to << "\n";
 21    hanoi(n - 1, via, to, from, moves, print);
 22}
 23
 24// Permutations by swapping (in place, with undo = backtracking pattern).
 25// ADAPT: replace the print by whatever you do with a full permutation.
 26void permute(std::vector<int> &a, size_t k, long long &count, bool print)
 27{
 28    if(k == a.size())
 29    {
 30        ++count;
 31        if(print)
 32        {
 33            std::cout << " ";
 34            for(int x : a)
 35                std::cout << ' ' << x;
 36            std::cout << "\n";
 37        }
 38        return;
 39    }
 40    for(size_t i = k; i < a.size(); ++i)
 41    {
 42        std::swap(a[k], a[i]);          // set
 43        permute(a, k + 1, count, print);
 44        std::swap(a[k], a[i]);          // cancel
 45    }
 46}
 47
 48// Permutations in lexicographic order using the standard library.
 49long long permuteStl(std::vector<int> a)
 50{
 51    std::sort(a.begin(), a.end());      // next_permutation needs sorted input to see all
 52    long long n = 0;
 53    do
 54    {
 55        ++n;
 56    } while(std::next_permutation(a.begin(), a.end()));
 57    return n;
 58}
 59
 60// Subsets (power set): for each item either skip it or take it.
 61void subsets(const std::vector<int> &items, size_t i, std::vector<int> &current,
 62             std::vector<std::vector<int>> &out)
 63{
 64    if(i == items.size())
 65    {
 66        out.push_back(current);
 67        return;
 68    }
 69    subsets(items, i + 1, current, out);        // skip item i
 70    current.push_back(items[i]);                // take item i   (set)
 71    subsets(items, i + 1, current, out);
 72    current.pop_back();                         //               (cancel)
 73}
 74
 75// Same with a bitmask: bit j of mask says "item j is in".
 76std::vector<std::vector<int>> subsetsMask(const std::vector<int> &items)
 77{
 78    std::vector<std::vector<int>> out;
 79    const unsigned int total = 1u << items.size();   // fine up to ~25 items
 80    for(unsigned int mask = 0; mask < total; ++mask)
 81    {
 82        std::vector<int> s;
 83        for(size_t j = 0; j < items.size(); ++j)
 84            if(mask & (1u << j))
 85                s.push_back(items[j]);
 86        out.push_back(s);
 87    }
 88    return out;
 89}
 90
 91// Subset-sum: is there a subset of 'items' adding up to 'target'? (with early exit)
 92bool subsetSum(const std::vector<int> &items, size_t i, int target)
 93{
 94    if(target == 0)
 95        return true;
 96    if(i == items.size() || target < 0)
 97        return false;
 98    return subsetSum(items, i + 1, target - items[i]) || subsetSum(items, i + 1, target);
 99}
100
101// Memoization
102// Fibonacci: naive is exponential, memoised is linear.
103long long fibNaive(int n)
104{
105    if(n < 2)
106        return n;
107    return fibNaive(n - 1) + fibNaive(n - 2);
108}
109
110long long fibMemo(int n, std::unordered_map<int, long long> &memo)
111{
112    if(n < 2)
113        return n;
114    auto it = memo.find(n);
115    if(it != memo.end())
116        return it->second;
117    const long long r = fibMemo(n - 1, memo) + fibMemo(n - 2, memo);
118    memo[n] = r;                                // store before returning
119    return r;
120}
121
122// Number of ways to make 'amount' with coins (order does not matter), memo on (amount, idx).
123// ADAPT: key = every parameter that changes between calls.
124long long ways(int amount, size_t idx, const std::vector<int> &coins,
125               std::map<std::pair<int, size_t>, long long> &memo)
126{
127    if(amount == 0)
128        return 1;
129    if(amount < 0 || idx == coins.size())
130        return 0;
131    const std::pair<int, size_t> key(amount, idx);
132    auto it = memo.find(key);
133    if(it != memo.end())
134        return it->second;
135    const long long r = ways(amount - coins[idx], idx, coins, memo)   // use coin idx again
136                      + ways(amount, idx + 1, coins, memo);           // move on to next coin
137    memo[key] = r;
138    return r;
139}
140
141// Bottom-up dynamic programming, same result.
142long long fibBottomUp(int n)
143{
144    if(n < 2)
145        return n;
146    long long a = 0, b = 1;
147    for(int i = 2; i <= n; ++i)
148    {
149        const long long c = a + b;
150        a = b;
151        b = c;
152    }
153    return b;
154}
155

157{
158    std::cout << "Hanoi with 3 discs:\n";
159    long long moves = 0;
160    hanoi(3, 'A', 'C', 'B', moves, true);
161    std::cout << "3 discs -> " << moves << " moves\n";
162    moves = 0;
163    hanoi(16, 'A', 'C', 'B', moves, false);
164    std::cout << "16 discs -> " << moves << " moves (2^16-1 = 65535)\n";
165
166    std::cout << "Permutations of {1,2,3}:\n";
167    std::vector<int> a{1, 2, 3};
168    long long count = 0;
169    permute(a, 0, count, true);
170    std::vector<int> b{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7};
171    count = 0;
172    permute(b, 0, count, false);
173    std::cout << "7 elements -> " << count << " permutations (5040), next_permutation says "
174              << permuteStl(b) << "\n";

176    const std::vector<int> items{1, 2, 3};
177    std::vector<std::vector<int>> all;
178    std::vector<int> cur;
179    subsets(items, 0, cur, all);
180    std::cout << "subsets of {1,2,3}: " << all.size() << " (mask version: "
181              << subsetsMask(items).size() << ")\n";
182    for(const auto &s : all)
183    {
184        std::cout << "  {";
185        for(size_t i = 0; i < s.size(); ++i)

190    std::cout << "subset of {3,34,4,12,5,2} summing to 9: "
191              << (subsetSum(nums, 0, 9) ? "yes" : "no") << ", to 30: "
192              << (subsetSum(nums, 0, 30) ? "yes" : "no") << "\n";
193
194    std::unordered_map<int, long long> memo;
195    std::cout << "fib(30) naive = " << fibNaive(30) << ", memo = " << fibMemo(30, memo)
196              << ", fib(80) memo = " << fibMemo(80, memo)
197              << ", bottom-up = " << fibBottomUp(80) << "\n";
198
199    std::map<std::pair<int, size_t>, long long> wmemo;
200    const std::vector<int> coins{1, 2, 5};
201    std::cout << "ways to make 100 with {1,2,5}: " << ways(100, 0, coins, wmemo)
202              << " (expected 541)\n";
203    return 0;
204}

CMakeLists templateLINK

# CMakeLists_template.txt - copy to your project folder as "CMakeLists.txt" and edit.
#
# Typical use (out-of-source build):
#     mkdir build && cd build
#     cmake ..                      # Release by default (fast)
#     cmake -DSANITIZE=ON ..        # debug build with address + undefined-behaviour checks
#     cmake -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Debug ..   # plain debug (for gdb)
#     make                          # or: cmake --build .
#     ./my_program
#
# ADAPT: project name, source files, optional libraries.

# Oldest CMake version this file is written for. 3.10 is on every lab PC.
cmake_minimum_required(VERSION 3.10)

# Project name + language. ADAPT: name.
project(my_project LANGUAGES CXX)

# language standard
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD 17)
set(CMAKE_CXX_STANDARD_REQUIRED ON)     # fail instead of silently falling back to older
set(CMAKE_CXX_EXTENSIONS OFF)           # -std=c++17 instead of -std=gnu++17

# build type: Release unless set otherwise
# Without this, CMake builds with NO optimisation (very slow for A*, GA, minimax).
if(NOT CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE AND NOT CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Release CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
endif()

# option: sanitizers
# cmake -DSANITIZE=ON ..  adds -g (debug info) and the two sanitizers:
#   address   : out-of-bounds, use-after-free, leaks
#   undefined : signed overflow, bad shifts, null deref ...
# Slower program, but it tells you the exact line of a crash. Do not combine with valgrind.
option(SANITIZE "Build with -g -fsanitize=address,undefined" OFF)
if(SANITIZE)
  set(CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE Debug CACHE STRING "Build type" FORCE)
  add_compile_options(-g -fno-omit-frame-pointer -fsanitize=address,undefined)
  # the sanitizer runtime must also be given to the linker (works on any CMake version)
  set(CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS "${CMAKE_EXE_LINKER_FLAGS} -fsanitize=address,undefined")
endif()

# warnings (GCC / Clang)
# Read them: most exam bugs (unused variable, sign compare, missing return) show up here.
if(CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER_ID MATCHES "GNU|Clang")
  add_compile_options(-Wall -Wextra)
endif()

# your program
# ADAPT: executable name and the list of .cpp files. Headers do not need to be listed.
add_executable(my_program
  main.cpp
  # solver.cpp
  # grid.cpp
)

# Where #include "..." and <...> of your own headers are searched. ADAPT or delete.
# target_include_directories(my_program PRIVATE ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/include)

# optional libraries: used only if installed
# find_package(... QUIET) never stops the configuration. We test the _FOUND variable and,
# if present, link the library and define a macro so the code can use #ifdef USE_OPENCV.

# OpenCV (images, maze display). No REQUIRED -> no error when absent.
find_package(OpenCV QUIET)
if(OpenCV_FOUND)
  message(STATUS "OpenCV found: ${OpenCV_VERSION}")
  target_include_directories(my_program PRIVATE ${OpenCV_INCLUDE_DIRS})
  target_link_libraries(my_program PRIVATE ${OpenCV_LIBS})
  target_compile_definitions(my_program PRIVATE USE_OPENCV)
else()
  message(STATUS "OpenCV not found: building without it")
endif()

# yaml-cpp (reading .yaml configuration files).
find_package(yaml-cpp QUIET)
if(yaml-cpp_FOUND OR YAML_CPP_FOUND)
  message(STATUS "yaml-cpp found")
  # Newer versions export the target yaml-cpp, older ones only a variable.
  if(TARGET yaml-cpp)
    target_link_libraries(my_program PRIVATE yaml-cpp)
  else()
    target_include_directories(my_program PRIVATE ${YAML_CPP_INCLUDE_DIR})
    target_link_libraries(my_program PRIVATE ${YAML_CPP_LIBRARIES})
  endif()
  target_compile_definitions(my_program PRIVATE USE_YAML)
else()
  message(STATUS "yaml-cpp not found: building without it")
endif()

# Threads (only if you use std::thread).
# find_package(Threads REQUIRED)
# target_link_libraries(my_program PRIVATE Threads::Threads)

# copy data files next to the executable (optional)
# file(COPY ${CMAKE_SOURCE_DIR}/data DESTINATION ${CMAKE_BINARY_DIR})

# several executables sharing code (optional)
# add_library(common STATIC common.cpp)
# add_executable(prog1 prog1.cpp)
# target_link_libraries(prog1 PRIVATE common)

 6
 7void Cell::init(uint row, uint col, std::array<Cell, 81> &grid, uint digit)
 8{
 9  if(digit)
10  {
11    this->digit_ = digit;
12    // no candidates, we know this one
13  }
14  else
15  {
16    candidates_.resize(9);
17    std::iota(candidates_.begin(), candidates_.end(), 1);
18  }
19
20  const auto cellPtr = [&grid](uint row, uint col) -> Cell*
21  {return grid.data() + 9*row + col;};
22
23  // register neighboors
24  const uint quad_row = 3*(row/3);
25  const uint quad_col = 3*(col/3);
26  auto nb{neighboors_.begin()};
27  for(uint ax = 0; ax < 9; ++ax)
28  {
29    // same colum, different row
30    if(ax != row)
31      *(nb++) = cellPtr(ax,col);
32    // same row, different column
33    if(ax != col)
34      *(nb++) = cellPtr(row, ax);
35    // same 3x3 sub-square
36    const uint r = quad_row + ax / 3;
37    const uint c = quad_col + ax % 3;
38    if(r != row && c != col)
39      *(nb++) = cellPtr(r, c);
40  }
41}

47{
48    if (!digit_)
49    {
50        bool in = (std::find(candidates_.begin(), candidates_.end(), guess) != candidates_.end());
51        if(in || pruned_count_[guess]!=0)
52        {
53            eraseCandidate(guess);
54            pruned_count_[guess]++;
55        }
56    }

59void Cell::restore(uint guess)
60{
61    if (!digit_ && pruned_count_[guess]!=0)
62    {
63        pruned_count_[guess]--;
64        if (pruned_count_[guess]==0)
65        {
66            candidates_.push_back(guess);
67        }
68    }
69}

72void Cell::set(uint guess)
73{
74    digit_ = guess;
75    for (int i = 0; i<neighboors_.size(); i++)
76    {
77        neighboors_[i]->prune(guess);
78    }
79}
80
81void Cell::cancel()
82{
83    for (int i = 0; i<neighboors_.size(); i++)
84    {
85        neighboors_[i]->restore(digit_);
86    }
87    digit_ = 0;
88}

 80/// main backtracking function
 81bool Grid::solveNextCell()
 82{
 83
 84  // TODO check if the grid is already full
 85  if(std::all_of(cells.begin(), cells.end(), Cell::isAssigned))
 86    return true;
 87
 88  // identify next cell to go, it is just the best under whatever bestNextCell considers
 89  auto &next_cell{*std::min_element(cells.begin(), cells.end(), bestNextCell)};
 90
 91  // just a check, it is meaningless to continue with an already solved cell
 92  if(next_cell.digit())
 93    throw std::runtime_error("Next cell already has a digit");
 94
 95  // TODO implement backtracking algorithm candidate loop

100          guesses++;
101      print(&next_cell);  // to display the picked guess
102      if(solveNextCell())
103      {
104          return true;
105      }
106      next_cell.cancel();
107      cancels++;
108      print(&next_cell, true);  // to display this guess was reset
109  }
